# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal,…185 tokens truncated… part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.

def structured(msg, round_):
    """A supplier e-mail in the structured shape of the /moves path."""
    sheet = (msg["term_sheets"] or [{}])[0]
    return {
        "offer_id": sheet.get("term_sheet_id"),
        "round": round_,
        "status": msg["status"],
        "terms": sheet.get("terms", {}),
        "missing_fields": msg["missing_fields"],
        "claims": [],
        "claim_results": msg["claim_results"],
        "signals": SIGNALS,
        "text": msg["body"],
    }


class Fail(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status, detail, headers=None):
        self.status, self.detail, self.headers = status, detail, headers


class Sim:
    """The arena's state and its one scripted supplier. One lock serialises every call."""

    def __init__(self, cases, facts=None, event_code="sim", clock=time.time, no_clock=False):
        self.cases, self.facts, self.code, self.clock = cases, facts or {}, event_code, clock
        self.no_clock = no_clock  # no 60-second rule: to try the API by hand
        self.teams, self.sessions, self.replies, self.calls = {}, {}, {}, {}
        self.ids, self.lock = itertools.count(1), threading.Lock()

    # -- the scripted supplier -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def _mail(self, s, th, status, stated, text, files=()):
        th["n"] += 1
        th.update(status=status, stated=stated, offer_id=f"offer:{th['key']}-{th['round']}")
        s["offers"][th["offer_id"]] = stated
        sheets = [] if status == "walked_away" else [{"term_sheet_id": th["offer_id"], "terms": stated}]
        msg = {
            "thread_id": f"thread:{s['case']['case_id'][5:]}:{th['key']}",
            "message_id": f"msg:{th['key']}-{th['round']}-{th['n']}",
            "in_reply_to": None,
            "from": f"sales@{th['key']}",
            "subject": f"Re: {s['case']['title']}",
            "body": f"Simulated supplier. {text}",
            "refs": [],
            "action": None,
            "term_sheets": sheets,
            "status": status,
            "signals": SIGNALS,
            "claim_results": [],
            "missing_fields": sorted(set(s["case"]["negotiable"]) - set(stated)),
            "attachments": [],
        }
        for kind in files:
            att = f"att:{th['key']}-{th['round']}-{kind.split('.')[0]}"
            s["files"][att] = (kind, dict(stated), dict(th["standard"]))
            msg["attachments"].append(
                {"attachment_id": att, "name": kind, "type": kind[-4:].strip("."), "content_b64": None}
            )
        th["messages"].append(msg)
        return msg

    def _answer(self, s, th, msg, sheets):
        results = []
        for i, ref in enumerate(list(dict.fromkeys(msg.get("refs", []) + ID_RE.findall(msg.get("body", ""))))[:3]):
            known = ref in self.facts or ref in s["case"].get("facts", {}) or ref in s["offers"]
            # a rival's quote may be cited to every bidder: it counts once per supplier, the rest once per case
            seen = (th["key"], ref) if ref.startswith(("quote:", "offer:")) else ref
            result = "contradicted" if not known else "duplicate" if seen in s["used"] else "verified"
            results.append({"index": i, "result": result})
            if known:
                s["used"].add(seen)
        files = ["cost-breakdown.xlsx"] if "breakdown" in msg.get("body", "").lower() else []
        price = round(max(th["opening"] * FLOOR, th["stated"]["unit_price"] - th["opening"] * STEP), 2)
        best = max(sheets, key=lambda t: t["unit_price"]) if sheets else None
        if best is None:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, th["status"], th["stated"], "We keep our offer.", files)
        elif best["unit_price"] >= price:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "agreed", best, "We agree.", [*files, "quote.pdf"])
        elif th["status"] == "final_offer":
            th["closed"] = "walked_away"
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "walked_away", th["stated"], "We end here.")
        elif th["round"] >= FINAL_ROUND:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "final_offer", {"unit_price": price}, "Final offer.", [*files, "quote.pdf"])
        else:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "open", {"unit_price": price}, "Our counter-offer.", files)
            while s["status"] == "open" and not th["closed"] and self.clock() > th["last_at"] + MOVE_S:
                th["last_at"] += MOVE_S
                th["round"] += 1
                th["timeouts"] += 1
                th["late"].append({"offer_id": th["offer_id"], "status": th["status"], "terms": th["stated"]})
                if th["timeouts"] >= 3 or th["round"] >= s["case"]["round_limit"]:
                    th["closed"] = "timeout"
                late.add(sup)
        self._settle(s, "timeout")
        return late

    def _settle(self, s, reason):
        if s["status"] == "open" and all(th["closed"] for th in s["threads"].values()):
            self._end(s, reason, None)

    def _end(self, s, reason, sup):
        case, ths = s["case"], s["threads"]
        c_open = min(total_cost(case, {"unit_price": th["opening"]}, th["standard"]) for th in ths.values())
        # the best this script would ever accept: its floor price, any allowed values of the other terms
        options = [case["term_options"].get(f) or [None] for f in case["negotiable"][1:]]
        c_best = min(
            total_cost(
                case,
                {
                    **dict(zip(case["negotiable"][1:], combo, strict=True)),
                    "unit_price": round(th["opening"] * FLOOR, 2),
                },
            )
            for th in ths.values()
            for combo in itertools.product(*options)
        )
        alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
        c_alt = total_cost(case, alt["terms"]) if alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") else None
        r = {
            "ended": True,
            "deal": False,
            "supplier_id": None,
            "offer_id": None,
            "terms": None,
            "c_open": c_open,
            "c_deal": None,
            "c_alt": c_alt,
            "c_best": c_best,
            "score": score(c_open, c_alt, c_best) if c_alt else 0.0,
            "must_haves_ok": None,
            "cost_breakdown": None,
            "trace": [],
        }
        if sup:
            t = closing_terms(case, ths[sup]["stated"], ths[sup]["standard"])
            r.update(
                deal=True,
                supplier_id=sup,
                offer_id=ths[sup]["offer_id"],
                terms=t,
                c_deal=total_cost(case, t),
                must_haves_ok=must_haves_ok(case, t),
                cost_breakdown=cost_breakdown(case, t),
            )
            r["score"] = score(c_open, r["c_deal"], c_best) if r["must_haves_ok"] else 0.0
        s.update(status="ended", end_reason=reason, result=r)
        for th in ths.values():
            th["closed"] = th["closed"] or reason

    def message(self, team, sid, sup, msg):
        s = self.session(team, sid)
        if s["status"] != "open":
            raise Fail(409, f"the session has ended: {s['end_reason']}")
        if sup not in s["threads"]:
            raise Fail(422, f"{sup} is not a supplier in this case")
        th, action = s["threads"][sup], msg.get("action") or {}
        if action.get("type") == "walk_away":
            self._end(s, "walked_away", None)
            note = {"body": "Simulated supplier. Understood - no deal.", "term_sheets": [], "attachments": []}
            return {**th["messages"][-1], **note, "result": _public(s["result"])}
        if sup in s["late"]:
            raise Fail(409, f"{LATE}; GET the thread for the supplier's answer")
        if th["closed"]:
            raise Fail(409, f"the thread with {sup} has ended: {th['closed']}")
        if action.get("type") == "accept":

            "subject": f"Re: {s['case']['title']}",
            "body": f"Simulated supplier. {text}",
            "refs": [],
            "action": None,
            "term_sheets": sheets,
            "status": status,
            "signals": SIGNALS,
            "claim_results": [],
            "missing_fields": sorted(set(s["case"]["negotiable"]) - set(stated)),
            "attachments": [],

        for kind in files:

I found one more timing gap: the agent wasn’t using the “next round must fit” check before 360 seconds. It now closes earlier when the measured round duration requires it.

The test suite has grown to 188 passing tests. I’m also checking the menus after the final guards run, so a two-option step can’t be recorded as a choice after one option is removed.

Automatic approval review rejected the simulator run with model calls, citing possible private-data disclosure. I ran the code-only simulator instead. The kit’s attribution file identifies the company data as synthetic and public, so I’ll provide that evidence when requesting the model-backed runs again.

Both sandbox cases ended in deals, and all three local simulator cases passed. The hosted baseline has matched the rounded P02 and P04 targets so far. P01 is below target: its logs show that the agent rejected higher unit prices even when a later effective date made the package cheaper overall. I’m investigating that restriction and whether price-round menus preserve settled terms.

The first hosted batch is complete: all 10 cases ended in deals, with a 64.73/100 mean and three targets matched. P05 had timeouts in one supplier thread, although the case still closed within the limit; I’m investigating that too.

The first fixes exposed a regression caused by treating `0` and `0.0` as different locked values. That’s corrected. I’m checking the fixes against recorded replies before another full run, and the report will distinguish verified improvements from remaining shortfalls.

Thanks—that authorizes the model-backed runs. I’ll run the configured model through the simulator first, then all 10 hosted cases. The code-only results remain useful as a fallback benchmark, and I’ll report them separately.

"""Reproducible rehearsals with results, full sessions, threads and a target table.

python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate --set sandbox --out runs/spec-sandbox
python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate --sim --out runs/spec-sim
python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate --set practice --parallel 5 --out runs/spec-practice
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import os
import socket
import statistics
import subprocess
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from pathlib import Path

from ..agents.spec import SpecAgent, make
from ..cli import load_env
from ..client import ArenaClient
from ..data import DataPackage
from ..play import RemoteTable, hosted, play

TARGETS = {"P01": .941, "P02": .507, "P03": .919, "P04": .860, "P05": .781,
           "P07": .773, "P08": .549, "P10": .671, "P11": .710, "P18": .453}


def write_json(path, data):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def audit(threads):
    replies, contradicted, timed_out, missing_company = [], [], [], []
    for sid, events in threads.items():
        for msg in events:
            if msg.get("from") == "buyer":
                if msg.get("body") and "Hollerau" not in msg["body"]:
                    missing_company.append(sid)
            else:
                replies.append(msg.get("status"))
                contradicted += [r for r in msg.get("claim_results") or [] if r.get("result") == "contradicted"]
                if "timeout" in (msg.get("body") or "").lower():
                    timed_out.append(sid)
    return {"reply_statuses": replies, "contradicted": contradicted,
            "timeout_mentions": timed_out, "buyer_without_company": missing_company}


def evaluate(client, cases, out, package, parallel=5, no_model=False):
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)  # never replace an earlier experiment
    files = sorted(Path("arena_kit").rglob("*.py"))
    metadata = {
        "started": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"),
        "git_head": subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip(),
        "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(b"".join(str(p).encode() + p.read_bytes() for p in files)).hexdigest(),
        "model": None if no_model else os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL"),
        "provider": None if no_model else os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER"),
        "cases": [c["case_id"] for c in cases],
    }
    write_json(out / "metadata.json", metadata)
    results = {}

    def one(case):
        cid = case["case_id"]
        table = RemoteTable(client, case)
        agent = SpecAgent(package=package, log_dir=out / "logs") if no_model else make(package)
        agent.log_dir = out / "logs"
        started = time.monotonic()
        record = {"case_id": cid}
        try:
            result = play(table, cid, agent)
            record.update(result=result, wall_s=round(time.monotonic() - started, 2), session_id=table.session_id)
            if table.session_id:
                state = client.session(table.session_id)
                threads = {sid: client.thread(table.session_id, sid) for sid in case["suppliers"]}
                record.update(session=state, threads=threads,
                              audit=audit({s: t["messages"] for s, t in threads.items()}))
        except Exception as error:
            record.update(error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}", session_id=table.session_id)
            logging.exception("%s failed", cid)
        finally:
            agent.pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
        write_json(out / f"{cid.split(':')[-1]}.json", record)
        score = (record.get("result") or {}).get("score")
        print(f"{cid}: deal={(record.get('result') or {}).get('deal')} score={score} "
              f"elapsed={record.get('wall_s')} error={record.get('error')}", flush=True)
        return cid, record

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(parallel, 10)) as pool:
        pending = [pool.submit(one, c) for c in cases]
        for future in as_completed(pending):
            cid, record = future.result()
            results[cid] = record
            write_json(out / "results.json", results)
    lines = ["# SpecAgent evaluation", "",
             "| Case | Score | Target | Meets rounded target | Deal | Seconds from open |",
             "|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|"]
    scores = []
    for cid, record in sorted(results.items()):
        r = record.get("result") or {}
        score, target = r.get("score"), TARGETS.get(cid.split(":")[-1])
        if score is not None:
            scores.append(score)
        logs = [x for x in agent_logs(out, cid) if x.get("event") == "result"]
        elapsed = logs[-1].get("elapsed") if logs else None
        passed = "—" if target is None or score is None else str(round(score, 3) >= target)
        lines.append(f"| {cid} | {score if score is not None else '—'} | {target or '—'} | {passed} | "
                     f"{r.get('deal')} | {elapsed} |")
    if scores:
        lines += ["", f"Mean score: {statistics.mean(scores):.6f} ({100 * statistics.mean(scores):.2f}/100)."]
    (out / "summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return results


def agent_logs(out, cid):
    return [json.loads(line) for p in sorted((out / "logs").glob(f"*_{cid.replace(':', '_')}.jsonl"))
            for line in p.read_text().splitlines()]


def main():
    load_env()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--set", default="practice", choices=["practice", "sandbox"])
    ap.add_argument("--sim", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--ids", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--no-model", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--capture-session", help="capture an existing ended session; requires exactly one --ids case")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(message)s")
    logging.getLogger("httpx").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    package = DataPackage(os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA", "data/package"))
    package.lookup("")
    server = None
    if args.sim:
        import uvicorn

        from ..sim import Sim, create_app, load_cases

        sock = socket.socket()
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{sock.getsockname()[1]}"
        state = Sim(load_cases(), package.facts)
        server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(state), log_level="error"))
        thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, kwargs={"sockets": [sock]}, daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        while not server.started:
            time.sleep(.01)
        client = ArenaClient(url, rate=9)
        key = client.register("SpecAgent rehearsal", "sim")["api_key"]
        client = ArenaClient(url, key)
    else:
        client = ArenaClient()
        print(json.dumps({"quota": client.me().get("practice")}), flush=True)
    try:
        cases = hosted(client.cases(args.set))
        if args.ids:
            ids = {i if i.startswith("case:") else f"case:{i}" for i in args.ids}
            cases = [c for c in cases if c["case_id"] in ids]
            if {c["case_id"] for c in cases} != ids:
                raise ValueError("one or more requested cases are unavailable")
        if args.capture_session:
            if len(cases) != 1:
                raise ValueError("capture requires exactly one case")
            case = cases[0]
            state = client.session(args.capture_session)
            if state.get("case_id") != case["case_id"] or state.get("status") != "ended":
                raise ValueError("capture session must be ended and match the requested case")
            threads = {sid: client.thread(args.capture_session, sid) for sid in case["suppliers"]}
            args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
            record = {"case_id": case["case_id"], "session_id": args.capture_session, "session": state,
                      "result": state.get("result"), "threads": threads,
                      "audit": audit({s: t["messages"] for s, t in threads.items()})}
            write_json(args.out / f"{case['case_id'].split(':')[-1]}.json", record)
        else:
            evaluate(client, cases, args.out, package, args.parallel, args.no_model)
    finally:
        if server:
            server.should_exit = True


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# SpecAgent design decisions

The implementation follows `NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md`. This file collects choices previously
recorded only in docstrings and records how requirements that overlap are reconciled.
Code controls prices, term sheets, accept/walk decisions, claims and deadlines. The model profiles
suppliers, extracts what they said and writes the surrounding email text. Every model call has a
deadline and a code fallback.

## Rule precedence

| Overlap | Decision and reason |
|---|---|
| R4.1 vs R13.10 anchors | Use the deeper cut: leverage 15%, routine 10%, quality 8%, stabilise 6%, secure supply 5%; RFQs add 4 points. Apply the current-price/fair-price candidates and credibility limits afterwards. The relationship cost minimum is a floor, rather than an independent second anchor. |
| R5.2 reciprocity vs R12.5 15% steps | The 15% gap rule determines the planned step; reciprocity caps it when the supplier moved less. The 0.4% visible-step minimum wins over that cap, as R5.2 explicitly specifies. A nonmoving supplier gets one hold, then a real step. |
| R5.4 vs no retreat | Continue negotiating while a supplier is still moving, but do not ask below our previous target merely because the supplier improved. Supplier and alternative caps can still lower the target. |
| R6 menus vs R13.1 sequential terms | After coverage, heavy terms use a single-term equal-cost menu. Price rounds use the reference/give/decoy menu. A supplier ask may replace that menu with two clear trade packages. |
| R13.1 goal order vs R12.7 payment probe | A payment term worth stepping goes first, so the first menu also reveals payment preference. Remaining terms follow goal priority, then EUR weight; at most three terms. |
| R13.3 reopen vs R13.4 choice | A costly term gets at most one reopen. A menu with fewer than two credible packages is skipped and never recorded as a step or a lock. Its best value stays available in price rounds. |
| R12.12 final offer vs continued steps | A valid final offer closes at once. Only an unacceptable final gets one repair at its own price. Tone, walk risk and deadlock are never independent close rules. |
| R12.16 wait for rivals vs R13.16 60 seconds | Wait only until 45 seconds after the chosen supplier's reply, leaving 15 seconds to accept. A slow POST is polled from the thread after 3 seconds; waiting 70 seconds could itself exceed the reply clock. |
| R11.14 vs R11.15 clock | No new counter after 360 seconds, and no counter earlier if its estimated round cannot finish by 420. Writer time is also capped by that remaining round budget. Clock starts immediately after session open, before document reading/preparation. A shorter wave moves both marks earlier; zero seconds forces a close. |

## Cost estimates and prices

Supplier full cost comes from its breakdown, otherwise should-cost / 1.02, otherwise opening / 1.10.
For an RFQ whose bids are below should-cost, the lowest opening bid replaces stale should-cost as
the fallback estimate. Later concessions cannot disable the margin penalty: market calibration uses
opening bids, not the lowest price reached during negotiation. Only stabilise and secure-supply
goals include the supplier margin penalty.

A missing alternative (`kind: none`) leaves the accept ceiling infinite. A real alternative is
priced with its actual terms. Offers must beat it both with the estimated supplier penalty and
without it. Coverage is requested when it lowers cost; subsequent packages cannot reduce committed
coverage. Coverage repair can explicitly restore the full horizon and annual need.

Without a margin penalty, solve price from the linear cost function. With it, use golden-section
search for the cost minimum and bisection above that minimum. Prices must use two decimals, so the
literal R13.8 “within EUR 1” is often mathematically impossible: changing the price by EUR 0.01 on
189,600 units changes spend by EUR 1,896. Tests therefore use max(EUR 1, EUR 0.005 × committed units)
for rounding error. This is a documented deviation, not a claim of literal compliance.

## Evidence and wording

Practice ranges are warnings, not replacement values: a valid case with an unusual interest rate
must use that rate. Missing/invalid fields receive defensive defaults; every warning is logged.
Unknown case types use their actual negotiable fields; unknown goals use the routine playbook.

Prose alternatives inherit unchanged terms from the main offer before revealed prices are computed.
They cannot be accepted by an invented offer ID: packages found only in prose are offered back for
confirmation. An ambiguous index clause is skipped. Dates and all numeric leaves returned by the
analyst must occur in the supplier's text, and nonfinite figures are rejected.

Index arguments use two months of one series, twelve months apart, ending in the most recent
twelve-month window of the frozen September 2026 data. Missing endpoints or old windows produce no
claim. Positive changes are excluded unless below half the supplier's requested increase. Each data
ID counts once per case; rival quote/offer IDs count once per supplier. Hidden-case facts override
package facts and also participate in volatility checks. A series moving more than 15% is excluded
from offered index clauses.

Code writes the options directly from the sheets, answers volume questions and inserts checked
claims. Lint drops leaking sentences, data IDs and unsupported figures, including small integers.
Personal salutations require a name in supplier emails; otherwise use the company name. Model
wording cannot introduce terms or change the action.

## Rehearsal and practical limits

`python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate` saves full sessions, thread histories, decision logs, a source
fingerprint and a score table in a new directory. `--sim` runs all three local cases over HTTP with
the clock enabled; `--set sandbox` plays D01/D02; `--set practice` selects hosted cases only. The
default parallelism is five cases, below the ten-open-session API limit.

Targets in the requirements are rounded to three decimals (for example the historical P01 score
0.940823 is written as 0.941). Evaluation compares three-decimal scores and retains exact raw values.
A historical team best is not evidence that this agent reached that target. The final report must
distinguish previous bests, current results, and unresolved shortfalls.

Clock guards use measured rounds capped at 90 seconds and the slowest of the last three plus ten
seconds. They cannot guarantee a server responds or commits an accept by 420 seconds during a
network outage. Hosted logs must be checked for actual closure times, refusals, timeouts and
contradicted claims; simulator scores validate plumbing, not hosted negotiation quality.

{"chunk_id":"f77b2d","wall_time_seconds":0.000011208,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":2127,"output":""""Reproducible rehearsals with results, full sessions, threads and a target table.

python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate --set sandbox --out runs/spec-sandbox
python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate --sim --out runs/spec-sim
python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate --set practice --parallel 5 --out runs/spec-practice
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import os
import socket
import statistics
import subprocess
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from pathlib import Path

from ..agents.spec import SpecAgent, make
from ..cli import load_env
from ..client import ArenaClient
from ..data import DataPackage
from ..play import RemoteTable, hosted, play

TARGETS = {"P01": .941, "P02": .507, "P03": .919, "P04": .860, "P05": .781,
           "P07": .773, "P08": .549, "P10": .671, "P11": .710, "P18": .453}


def write_json(path, data):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def audit(threads):
    replies, contradicted, timed_out, missing_company = [], [], [], []
    for sid, events in threads.items():
        for msg in events:
            if msg.get("from") == "buyer":
                if msg.get("body") and "Hollerau" not in msg["body"]:
                    missing_company.append(sid)
            else:
                replies.append(msg.get("status"))
                contradicted += [r for r in msg.get("claim_results") or [] if r.get("result") == "contradicted"]
                if "timeout" in (msg.get("body") or "").lower():
                    timed_out.append(sid)
    return {"reply_statuses": replies, "contradicted": contradicted,
            "timeout_mentions": timed_out, "buyer_without_company": missing_company}


def evaluate(client, cases, out, package, parallel=5, no_model=False):
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)  # never replace an earlier experiment
    files = sorted(Path("arena_kit").rglob("*.py"))
    metadata = {
        "started": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"),
        "git_head": subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip(),
        "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(b"".join(str(p).encode() + p.read_bytes() for p in files)).hexdigest(),
        "model": None if no_model else os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL"),
        "provider": None if no_model else os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER"),
        "cases": [c["case_id"] for c in cases],
    }
    write_json(out / "metadata.json", metadata)
    results = {}

    def one(case):
        cid = case["case_id"]
        table = RemoteTable(client, case)
        agent = SpecAgent(package=package, log_dir=out / "logs") if no_model else make(package)
        agent.log_dir = out / "logs"
        started = time.monotonic()
        record = {"case_id": cid}
        try:
            result = play(table, cid, agent)
            record.update(result=result, wall_s=round(time.monotonic() - started, 2), session_id=table.session_id)
            if table.session_id:
                state = client.session(table.session_id)
                threads = {sid: client.thread(table.session_id, sid) for sid in case["suppliers"]}
                record.update(session=state, threads=threads,
                              audit=audit({s: t["messages"] for s, t in threads.items()}))
        except Exception as error:
            record.update(error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}", session_id=table.session_id)
            logging.exception("%s failed", cid)
        finally:
            agent.pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
        write_json(out / f"{cid.split(':')[-1]}.json", record)
        score = (record.get("result") or {}).get("score")
        print(f"{cid}: deal={(record.get('result') or {}).get('deal')} score={score} "
              f"elapsed={record.get('wall_s')} error={record.get('error')}", flush=True)
        return cid, record

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(parallel, 10)) as pool:
        pending = [pool.submit(one, c) for c in cases]
        for future in as_completed(pending):
            cid, record = future.result()
            results[cid] = record
            write_json(out / "results.json", results)
    lines = ["# SpecAgent evaluation", "",
             "| Case | Score | Target | Meets rounded target | Deal | Seconds from open |",
             "|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|"]
    scores = []
    for cid, record in sorted(results.items()):
        r = record.get("result") or {}
        score, target = r.get("score"), TARGETS.get(cid.split(":")[-1])
        if score is not None:
            scores.append(score)
        logs = [x for x in agent_logs(out, cid) if x.get("event") == "result"]
        elapsed = logs[-1].get("elapsed") if logs else None
        passed = "—" if target is None or score is None else str(round(score, 3) >= target)
        lines.append(f"| {cid} | {score if score is not None else '—'} | {target or '—'} | {passed} | "
                     f"{r.get('deal')} | {elapsed} |")
    if scores:
        lines += ["", f"Mean score: {statistics.mean(scores):.6f} ({100 * statistics.mean(scores):.2f}/100)."]
    (out / "summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return results


def agent_logs(out, cid):
    return [json.loads(line) for p in sorted((out / "logs").glob(f"*_{cid.replace(':', '_')}.jsonl"))
            for line in p.read_text().splitlines()]


def main():
    load_env()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--set", default="practice", choices=["practice", "sandbox"])
    ap.add_argument("--sim", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--parallel", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--ids", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--no-model", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--capture-session", help="capture an existing ended session; requires exactly one --ids case")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(message)s")
    logging.getLogger("httpx").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
    package = DataPackage(os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA", "data/package"))
    package.lookup("")
    server = None
    if args.sim:
        import uvicorn

        from ..sim import Sim, create_app, load_cases

        sock = socket.socket()
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{sock.getsockname()[1]}"
        state = Sim(load_cases(), package.facts)
        server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(state), log_level="error"))
        thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, kwargs={"sockets": [sock]}, daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        while not server.started:
            time.sleep(.01)
        client = ArenaClient(url, rate=9)
        key = client.register("SpecAgent rehearsal", "sim")["api_key"]
        client = ArenaClient(url, key)
    else:
        client = ArenaClient()
        print(json.dumps({"quota": client.me().get("practice")}), flush=True)
    try:
        cases = hosted(client.cases(args.set))
        if args.ids:
            ids = {i if i.startswith("case:") else f"case:{i}" for i in args.ids}
            cases = [c for c in cases if c["case_id"] in ids]
            if {c["case_id"] for c in cases} != ids:
                raise ValueError("one or more requested cases are unavailable")
        if args.capture_session:
            if len(cases) != 1:
                raise ValueError("capture requires exactly one case")
            case = cases[0]
            state = client.session(args.capture_session)
            if state.get("case_id") != case["case_id"] or state.get("status") != "ended":
                raise ValueError("capture session must be ended and match the requested case")
            threads = {sid: client.thread(args.capture_session, sid) for sid in case["suppliers"]}
            args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
            record = {"case_id": case["case_id"], "session_id": args.capture_session, "session": state,
                      "result": state.get("result"), "threads": threads,
                      "audit": audit({s: t["messages"] for s, t in threads.items()})}
            write_json(args.out / f"{case['case_id'].split(':')[-1]}.json", record)
        else:
            evaluate(client, cases, args.out, package, args.parallel, args.no_model)
    finally:
        if server:
            server.should_exit = True


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"}

{"chunk_id":"f773d2","wall_time_seconds":0.000010375,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":1695,"output":"# SpecAgent design decisions

The implementation follows `NEW_AGENT_REQUIREMENTS.md`. This file collects choices previously
recorded only in docstrings and records how requirements that overlap are reconciled.
Code controls prices, term sheets, accept/walk decisions, claims and deadlines. The model profiles
suppliers, extracts what they said and writes the surrounding email text. Every model call has a
deadline and a code fallback.

## Rule precedence

| Overlap | Decision and reason |
|---|---|
| R4.1 vs R13.10 anchors | Use the deeper cut: leverage 15%, routine 10%, quality 8%, stabilise 6%, secure supply 5%; RFQs add 4 points. Apply the current-price/fair-price candidates and credibility limits afterwards. The relationship cost minimum is a floor, rather than an independent second anchor. |
| R5.2 reciprocity vs R12.5 15% steps | The 15% gap rule determines the planned step; reciprocity caps it when the supplier moved less. The 0.4% visible-step minimum wins over that cap, as R5.2 explicitly specifies. A nonmoving supplier gets one hold, then a real step. |
| R5.4 vs no retreat | Continue negotiating while a supplier is still moving, but do not ask below our previous target merely because the supplier improved. Supplier and alternative caps can still lower the target. |
| R6 menus vs R13.1 sequential terms | After coverage, heavy terms use a single-term equal-cost menu. Price rounds use the reference/give/decoy menu. A supplier ask may replace that menu with two clear trade packages. |
| R13.1 goal order vs R12.7 payment probe | A payment term worth stepping goes first, so the first menu also reveals payment preference. Remaining terms follow goal priority, then EUR weight; at most three terms. |
| R13.3 reopen vs R13.4 choice | A costly term gets at most one reopen. A menu with fewer than two credible packages is skipped and never recorded as a step or a lock. Its best value stays available in price rounds. |
| R12.12 final offer vs continued steps | A valid final offer closes at once. Only an unacceptable final gets one repair at its own price. Tone, walk risk and deadlock are never independent close rules. |
| R12.16 wait for rivals vs R13.16 60 seconds | Wait only until 45 seconds after the chosen supplier's reply, leaving 15 seconds to accept. A slow POST is polled from the thread after 3 seconds; waiting 70 seconds could itself exceed the reply clock. |
| R11.14 vs R11.15 clock | No new counter after 360 seconds, and no counter earlier if its estimated round cannot finish by 420. Writer time is also capped by that remaining round budget. Clock starts immediately after session open, before document reading/preparation. A shorter wave moves both marks earlier; zero seconds forces a close. |

## Cost estimates and prices

Supplier full cost comes from its breakdown, otherwise should-cost / 1.02, otherwise opening / 1.10.
For an RFQ whose bids are below should-cost, the lowest opening bid replaces stale should-cost as
the fallback estimate. Later concessions cannot disable the margin penalty: market calibration uses
opening bids, not the lowest price reached during negotiation. Only stabilise and secure-supply
goals include the supplier margin penalty.

A missing alternative (`kind: none`) leaves the accept ceiling infinite. A real alternative is
priced with its actual terms. Offers must beat it both with the estimated supplier penalty and
without it. Coverage is requested when it lowers cost; subsequent packages cannot reduce committed
coverage. Coverage repair can explicitly restore the full horizon and annual need.

Without a margin penalty, solve price from the linear cost function. With it, use golden-section
search for the cost minimum and bisection above that minimum. Prices must use two decimals, so the
literal R13.8 “within EUR 1” is often mathematically impossible: changing the price by EUR 0.01 on
189,600 units changes spend by EUR 1,896. Tests therefore use max(EUR 1, EUR 0.005 × committed units)
for rounding error. This is a documented deviation, not a claim of literal compliance.

## Evidence and wording

Practice ranges are warnings, not replacement values: a valid case with an unusual interest rate
must use that rate. Missing/invalid fields receive defensive defaults; every warning is logged.
Unknown case types use their actual negotiable fields; unknown goals use the routine playbook.

Prose alternatives inherit unchanged terms from the main offer before revealed prices are computed.
They cannot be accepted by an invented offer ID: packages found only in prose are offered back for
confirmation. An ambiguous index clause is skipped. Dates and all numeric leaves returned by the
analyst must occur in the supplier's text, and nonfinite figures are rejected.

Index arguments use two months of one series, twelve months apart, ending in the most recent
twelve-month window of the frozen September 2026 data. Missing endpoints or old windows produce no
claim. Positive changes are excluded unless below half the supplier's requested increase. Each data
ID counts once per case; rival quote/offer IDs count once per supplier. Hidden-case facts override
package facts and also participate in volatility checks. A series moving more than 15% is excluded
from offered index clauses.

Code writes the options directly from the sheets, answers volume questions and inserts checked
claims. Lint drops leaking sentences, data IDs and unsupported figures, including small integers.
Personal salutations require a name in supplier emails; otherwise use the company name. Model
wording cannot introduce terms or change the action.

## Rehearsal and practical limits

`python -m arena_kit.spec.evaluate` saves full sessions, thread histories, decision logs, a source
fingerprint and a score table in a new directory. `--sim` runs all three local cases over HTTP with
the clock enabled; `--set sandbox` plays D01/D02; `--set practice` selects hosted cases only. The
default parallelism is five cases, below the ten-open-session API limit.

Targets in the requirements are rounded to three decimals (for example the historical P01 score
0.940823 is written as 0.941). Evaluation compares three-decimal scores and retains exact raw values.
A historical team best is not evidence that this agent reached that target. The final report must
distinguish previous bests, current results, and unresolved shortfalls.

Clock guards use measured rounds capped at 90 seconds and the slowest of the last three plus ten
seconds. They cannot guarantee a server responds or commits an accept by 420 seconds during a
network outage. Hosted logs must be checked for actual closure times, refusals, timeouts and
contradicted claims; simulator scores validate plumbing, not hosted negotiation quality.
"}

"""Evaluation must not hide reply-clock violations behind a successful deal."""

from arena_kit.spec.evaluate import audit


def test_audit_reports_structured_timeouts_even_without_email_warning():
    report = audit({"sup:1": {
        "messages": [{"from": "supplier", "body": "Our final offer.", "status": "final_offer"}],
        "timeouts": [{"round": 2, "kind": "reply_clock"}],
    }})
    assert report["timeouts"] == [{"supplier_id": "sup:1", "timeout": {"round": 2, "kind": "reply_clock"}}]
    assert not report["timeout_mentions"]


def test_audit_checks_claims_company_and_timeout_text():
    report = audit({"sup:1": {"messages": [
        {"from": "buyer", "body": "Please confirm."},
        {"from": "supplier", "body": "Timeout warning", "status": "open",
         "claim_results": [{"result": "contradicted", "data_id": "bad"}]},
    ]}})
    assert report["buyer_without_company"] == ["sup:1"]
    assert report["contradicted"] == [{"result": "contradicted", "data_id": "bad"}]
    assert report["timeout_mentions"] == ["sup:1"]
    assert not report["timeouts"]

"""R11.2, R11.8 and R11.12: extraction is evidence, never invented numbers."""

import pytest
from spec_support import agent, case, opening

from arena_kit.spec.analyst import Intel, appears, clean_extraction
from arena_kit.spec.tactics import pick


def test_r11_2_drops_unstated_prices_days_dates_and_driver_shares():
    body = "We can offer EUR 137.00 with payment 30 days, from 1 April 2027. Energy rose 2.7%."
    parsed = {
        "prose_offers": [
            {"unit_price": 99, "payment_days": 30},
            {"unit_price": 137, "payment_days": 60, "effective_date": "2027-01-01",
             "other_terms": {"lead_time_days": 42, "incoterm": "DAP"}},
            {"unit_price": 137, "payment_days": 30, "effective_date": "2027-04-01"},
        ],
        "cost_drivers": [
            {"name": "energy", "change_pct": 2.7, "cost_share_pct": 40},
            {"name": "labour", "change_pct": 5, "cost_share_pct": 30},
        ],
    }
    result = clean_extraction(parsed, body, ["unit_price", "payment_days", "effective_date",
                                             "lead_time_days", "incoterm"])
    assert [o["terms"] for o in result["prose_offers"]] == [
        {"unit_price": 137.0},
        {"unit_price": 137.0, "payment_days": 30, "effective_date": "2027-04-01"},
    ]
    assert len(result["cost_drivers"]) == 1
    assert result["cost_drivers"][0]["share_pct"] is None


@pytest.mark.parametrize("number", [37, 13, float("nan"), float("inf")])
def test_r11_2_no_substring_or_nonfinite_figures(number):
    assert not appears(number, "EUR 137.00, payment 30 days")


def test_r11_2_cannot_truncate_price_or_invent_hint_figures():
    assert not appears(137, "EUR 137.90")
    assert not appears(3, "The index moved -3%.")
    assert appears(137, "EUR 137.00, payment 30 days")
    result = clean_extraction({"constraints": ["Only payment 30 days", "Only payment 14 days"],
                               "lever_hints": [{"field": "payment_days", "hint": "14 days"}]},
                              "Payment 30 days", ["payment_days"])
    assert result["constraints"] == ["Only payment 30 days"]
    assert result["lever_hints"] == []


def test_r11_8_locks_better_prose_offer_with_inherited_terms():
    c = case("case:P01", category_goal="leverage")
    sid = c["suppliers"][0]
    terms = {"unit_price": 138.55, "payment_days": 60, "effective_date": "2027-04-01"}
    threads = {sid: [opening(sid, terms, body="We can offer EUR 135.00 with payment 60 days.")]}
    a = agent(c, threads)
    state = a.state(threads, sid)
    got = a.lock_in(state)
    assert got and got[0] == {**terms, "unit_price": 135}
    states, views = a.views(threads)
    a.clock.t_open -= 361  # late, and the default 55-second round still fits
    move = a.late(states, views, sid)
    assert move.kind == "lock_in"
    decision = a.realise(move, states, threads, sid)
    assert decision["message"]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"] == got[0]
    assert "lock" in a.t[sid].flags


def test_r11_8_does_not_lock_expensive_or_must_have_breaking_prose():
    c = case("case:P05")
    sid = c["suppliers"][0]
    threads = {sid: [opening(sid, {"unit_price": 36, "payment_days": 60, "lead_time_days": 42})]}
    a = agent(c, threads)
    state = a.state(threads, sid)
    for terms in ({"unit_price": 40}, {"unit_price": 20, "lead_time_days": 52}):
        state["intel"].prose_offers = [{"terms": terms}]
        assert a.lock_in(state) is None


def test_r11_12_competitive_pressure_requires_real_competition():
    for first in (True, False):
        name, _ = pick(Intel("s"), {"first": first, "rfq": False, "rival_cheaper": False})
        assert name != "competitive_pressure"
    assert pick(Intel("s"), {"rival_cheaper": True})[0] == "competitive_pressure"


def test_tactic_respects_risk_and_annoyed_supplier():
    intel = Intel("s", tone=-2, walk_risk=0.5, relationship_style="relationship")
    assert pick(intel, {"supplier_held": True, "hold": True, "relationship": True})[0] == "appreciation_close"


def test_r11_15_agent_closes_before_starting_round_that_would_not_fit():
    c = case("case:P01", category_goal="leverage")
    sid = c["suppliers"][0]
    threads = {sid: [opening(sid, {"unit_price": 138.55, "payment_days": 60,
                                 "effective_date": "2027-04-01"})]}
    a = agent(c, threads)
    a.clock.t_open -= 330
    a.clock.rounds = [90]
    decision = a.decide(c, threads, sid)
    assert decision["message"]["action"]["type"] == "accept"


def test_r12_17_writer_skipped_when_reply_budget_is_under_ten_seconds():
    import time

    from spec_support import no_model

    c = case("case:P01", category_goal="leverage")
    sid = c["suppliers"][0]
    threads = {sid: [opening(sid, {"unit_price": 138.55, "payment_days": 60,
                                 "effective_date": "2027-04-01"})]}
    a = agent(c, threads)
    a.complete = no_model
    a.reply_at[sid] = time.monotonic() - 45
    decision = a.decide(c, threads, sid)
    assert decision["message"].get("term_sheets")

item.aggregated_output:
- **R12.2 Coverage lock.** Commit the full need for the full horizon from message 1 whenever the
  lever table says covering it lowers C (P08: 24 months on a 2-year need; 12-month packages scored
  0.08 vs 0.44 there; P10: the volume was cut below the must-have in 4/4 runs without it). Once our
  sheet A covers the need, no sheet we send covers less - not even one the model writes. Trust the
  table when coverage does **not** pay: P08's fallback EUR 5.72 was below the offer's 5.98.

### 12.2 Levers priced in euros

- **R12.3 Lever table** (`team/levers.py`). For the supplier's standing sheet, move every negotiable
  field to each allowed option, and the price by 1 %; the change in C is the lever's value in EUR and
  in EUR per unit (`price_equiv`). Ask only for levers worth at least 0.3 % of C (coverage always
  counts): suppliers price every demand in, at 3-7× its value for faster lead time or chargebacks -
  ask only what the need requires.
- **R12.4 Revealed lever prices.** When two of the supplier's sheets (main and alternative) differ in
  one term, that pair is its own price for the term (`revealed_slopes`). With it, a lever counts only
  if it saves us more than the supplier charges for it; on a tie (within EUR 1) take the option closest
  to the supplier's own value - no stricter ask than needed. Its payment slope is its cost of money
  (R2.2).

### 12.3 Anchor and steps

- **R12.5 Steps in C, at least 15 % of the gap.** Mined: messages without a step drew a final offer
  37 % of the time, steps of at least 15 % of the gap 17 %. TeamAgent's path gives 0 / 15 / 30 / 45 /
  60 % of the gap from anchor to the supplier's C by our 1st ... 5th message, never less than 15 % of
  what was left after our last message, and never above 0.997 × the supplier's C. In this agent the
  15 % is the size of the deadlock-breaking step (R5.3) and the floor of a step we choose to make;
  the reciprocity cap (R5.2) still limits our step when the supplier moved less.
- **R12.6 RFQ anchor only falls.** The anchor is the lowest price anyone has put on the table in the
  case, cut by the goal's share plus 4 points for competition; in an RFQ it may move down when a
  rival goes lower, never up (R4.4 otherwise).

### 12.4 Sheets

- **R12.7 Payment probe.** One sheet of the first menu varies payment days (to the supplier's own
  value, or to 30 days) at equal C: its pick reveals its cost of money (P05: 90/60/30 sheets; the
  bidder came back at 30 days and EUR 28.42).
- **R12.8 Index clause on the supplier's terms.** When the supplier insists on an index clause, offer
  its own series with the deadband that costs us least, never a 0 % deadband we can avoid (P08: its
  0 % became 5 % in the final offer).
- **R12.9 A floor per structure.** Each variant has its own price floor - faster payment is worth
  more to the supplier, so that sheet may go lower. A give worth more than the price room (e.g. half
  the need uncovered) is no offer.
- **R12.10 Never regress.** Never send a sheet that costs us as much as one the supplier has already
  offered (within 0.1 %). If nothing cheaper is left: offer back its earlier, cheaper sheet once, else
  accept.

### 12.5 Closing

- **R12.11 Accept ladder.** Accept from every sheet the supplier ever offered in every live thread -
  main sheets and alternatives - cheapest valid first; up to three earlier IDs (cheaper by 0.1 %+)
  before the latest ones; a refused accept changes nothing, try the next. Mined: the cheapest sheet
  ever offered was often not the one taken (P01 7/7 runs: 0.586 vs 0.550); 30 % of replies carry an
  alternative, 38 % of those are cheaper for us than the main sheet.
- **R12.12 A final offer is accepted at once.** Any message after a `final_offer` → walked away 8/8;
  accepting it → deal 38/38. Only when nothing on the table is acceptable (it breaks a must-have or
  loses to our alternative) send **one** repair message: its price, accepted, with the nearest
  must-have-keeping option and full coverage (`confirm_final`).
- **R12.13 `agreed` or stalled → its earlier cheaper sheet, once.** `agreed` only echoes our last
  sheet: if one of its earlier sheets costs us 0.3 % less, offer exactly those terms back first.
  Stalled = no cheaper offer over its last three replies after 3+ of our messages.

### 12.6 RFQ

- **R12.14 First message by code, with the rival.** In an RFQ the first message to each bidder goes
  out without waiting for the model (three model calls at once would miss the clock) and carries the
  cheapest valid rival offer: "A competing supplier has offered EUR X per unit (offer:...)" (P05).
- **R12.15 Idle hopeless threads.** With 3+ live bidders, stop writing to one whose best valid sheet
  is more than 8 % dearer than the best anywhere and that moved less than 1 % in its last reply.
- **R12.16 Wait before an accept.** Before accepting in an RFQ, wait for replies still in flight from
  other bidders - one of them may be cheaper.

### 12.7 Time and robustness

- **R12.17 Model time budget.** The model gets 50 s minus the time since the supplier's reply minus
  15 s for every other thread with a call in flight; under 10 s left, the planned move goes out
  without it.
- **R12.18 Runner** (`team/runner.py`, `team/final.py`): one worker per supplier thread; calls retried,
  and a send that may have landed is checked against the arena before it is repeated; a worker never
  dies on an error; a case is done only when the arena ended the session; before a wave cap, close on
  the accept ladder; a crashed runner resumes its open sessions; `--check` pre-flight and `--rehearse`
  on the sandbox.

### 12.8 Data hygiene

- **R12.19 Cash-short only from the supplier's own words**, never from our briefing labels or from
  its echo of our e-mail.
- **R12.20 Claims, sentence by sentence.** Drop a sentence whose IDs were all cited before (a repeat
  comes back `duplicate`: 18 % of TeamAgent's claims did before this rule); drop IDs the data does not have.
  Price-history claims (our past order prices) are context, not arguments: they "hold, but do not
  change our calculation" in 41 of 46 replies.
- **R12.21 Data attachment on request.** When the supplier asks for our figures ("which figures?",
  "send us the data", "verify this"), attach `our-figures.md`: every ID we cited with its values from
  the data package.

### Not taken from TeamAgent

- **The model proposing term sheets and accept/walk.** TeamAgent let the model re-mix the sheets and
  then clamped them back to the plan; here code decides every number (sections 5-7, R9.1). Its
  close rules (R12.11-R12.13) are code, and are taken.
- **The fixed 0/15/30/45/60 % schedule as the only concession rule**: the curve and reciprocity of
  section 5 stay; R12.5 sets the step size.

## 13. From the MESO agent

### 13.1 Settling terms one at a time

- **R13.1 Sequential equal-cost steps for the heavy terms.** After coverage is set (R12.2), rank the
  remaining non-price terms by how many EUR they move C (the playbook's terms first, R13.10), skip any
  under 0.2 % of C, keep at most 3. Each message varies **one** term across up to three packages that
  all cost us the same C; the value the supplier answers with is locked, and the next message varies
  the next term; when every term is locked, only price is left. This is how the R6 sheets are built in
  the first rounds; R6's give / ask / decoy sheets apply in the price rounds and to asked-for terms.
  P11: 300 ppm locked from a 300 / 800 / 1,500 menu → 0.710 twice.
- **R13.2 Option order in a step:** the best option for us first, then the one the supplier asked for
  (if any), its current value, the middle option, the rest - three at most, each a different package.
- **R13.3 Reopen a costly lock.** A term stepped only once whose locked value costs us more than 1 %
  of C against its best option gets one more step (P01: the earliest effective date was worth 3.5 %
  of C).
- **R13.4 A step needs a choice.** A step with fewer than two credible packages (the rest under the
  floor or not cheaper than the supplier's sheet) is not a step: keep the term open, move it to the
  price round with our best value, or skip it - never "lock" a heavy term by sending it alone (P01,
  0.159).
- **R13.5 A term the supplier prices itself is locked without a step** (`revealed`): when its
  e-mail offers two packages that differ in one term only - its sheet and an "Alternatively, with
  30 days: EUR ..." line - lock that term at the value that costs us less at the supplier's own
  prices.
- **R13.6 Read the supplier's prose alternatives** (`prose_alternatives`): "Alternatively, with
  <terms>: EUR <price> per unit" in English and German (Zahlungsziel, Lieferzeit,
  Preisgleitklausel), for payment days, effective date, lead time, volume, contract months, ppm,
  chargeback and Incoterm; a line whose index clause cannot be pinned to an option is skipped. These
  packages feed R12.11 (accept ladder) and R13.5.
- **R13.7 No identical resend.** If the next message would only repeat our last sheets, the thread
  is done (a repeat draws a final offer) - close by R7 or offer back an earlier, cheaper sheet once.

### 13.2 Correct numbers

- **R13.8 Solve the price exactly.** Every package is priced so its C equals the target, not by a
  rule of thumb:
  - without the supplier's margin charge C is linear in the price: `p = (target − C(0)) / (C(1) − C(0))`;
  - with it, C is convex in the price: find the cheapest price by golden-section search between 0.5×
    and 1.5× the supplier's price, and solve for the target by bisection on the side **above** it
    (a price below the cheapest one costs more and leaves the supplier weaker).
  Tests: each sheet of a step has the same C within EUR 1.
- **R13.9 Data arguments computed the way the arena checks them** (`claims.py`): an index change uses
  two months of one series at most 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data
  (frozen at 2026-09); figures rounded as the sentence states them, next to their IDs. Only arguments
  that argue our side are offered: an index that **rose** confirms the supplier's case and is kept out
  unless it rose less than half the increase asked for (P02, P04). Kinds: index changes, the weighted
  summary of the part's own cost drivers ("explain about +x %, not y %", no ID), a letter giving less
  notice than the contract requires, scorecard quality and delivery, rival quotes and offers,
  should-cost, forecast volume. Each ID once per case; a rival's offer once per supplier.

### 13.3 Playbook per category goal

- **R13.10 One engine, settings per goal** (`PLAYBOOK`):

  | Goal | Anchor (× opening) | Concede | Terms first | Index clause | Margin charge | Walk | Close gap |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | leverage | 0.85 | 0.85 | payment, index | any | no | yes | 0.5 % |
  | routine | 0.90 | 0.80 | contract months, payment | avoid | no | yes | 1.0 % |
  | stabilise | margin-optimal price | 0.80 | volume, contract months, payment | deadband ≥ 3 % | yes | no | 0.5 % |
  | secure_supply | 0.95 | 0.70 | volume, lead time, contract months | avoid | yes | no | 1.5 % |
  | quality_first | 0.92 | 0.80 | ppm, chargeback | avoid | no | yes | 0.5 % |

  The anchors here and in R4.1 must be reconciled into one table before implementation (R4.1's cuts
  come from BuyerAgent and are data-driven; these are MESO's fixed shares). "Walk: no" means:
  stabilise and secure_supply take the best sheet that beats the alternative rather than walk.
- **R13.11 No index clause on a volatile series.** Never offer an index clause on a series that moved
  more than 15 % in its last 12 months - a clause on it is a bet.
- **R13.12 Price-increase anchor:** in a price_increase case the anchor is the current price - no
  increase at all - when it is below the quote.
- **R13.13 Accept on a small gap:** once only price is left, accept when the supplier's C is within
  the playbook's close gap of our target.

### 13.4 The e-mail

- **R13.14 Code writes what must match the sheets** (`writing.py`): the options paragraph is built
  from the term sheets themselves (`describe`: price, payment, effective date, months, volume, lead
  time, index clause with series, share, deadband and base month, ppm, chargeback, Incoterm, tooling),
  so prose and sheets never disagree; code adds its own sentences (a volume commitment, an earlier
  offer taken up) and the signature.
- **R13.15 Lint before sending.** Drop any sentence of the model's that leaks urgency, a deadline, a
  budget, a missing alternative ("no other supplier", "single source", "line stop", "fallback"), our
  limit ("walk-away price", "maximum we", "best we can pay"), "total cost", "category goal" or
  "score"; that carries a data ID; or that states a figure found nowhere in the material. Salutation by
  name only if that name appears in the supplier's e-mails, else "Dear colleagues at <company>". A
  volume question ("which volume can you commit?") is answered by code with the number from our sheet.

### 13.5 Never lose a reply or an accept

- **R13.16 Reply and accept inside 60 s.** A slow POST reads the supplier's reply from the thread
  instead of waiting on the call, so the 60-second rule is not missed (P05 once lost two agreed deals
  to replies held back this way). In an RFQ a final offer that is the best on the table is accepted
  within 60 s of its reply, even while other threads are still talking - waiting for in-flight
  replies (R12.16) never runs past that clock (P05, meso3: accepted after 4.5 minutes → `409`, no deal).
  On a `422` for an accept (the offer moved on) reload the thread and decide again.
- **R13.17 Cached data layer.** Build the master data file once (`arena-build-master-data`) and cache
  each case's negotiation dossier per data revision, so preparation for a case is a cache hit
  (milliseconds) and the Sunday release is picked up automatically.

### Not taken from the MESO agent

- **Locking whatever the supplier picks on a heavy term**, without R13.3/R13.4 (P01, 0.159).
- **The fixed `(1 − concede^k)` curve as the only concession rule** - section 5 (curve, reciprocity,
  deadlock breaker) stays. R13.10's `concede` column is MESO's pace per goal, a reference for tuning
  section 5's horizon per goal.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests for R5.2-R5.4 (reciprocity, deadlock breaker, still-moving), R6.2-R6.5 (surplus,
  ask sheets, decoy, floor) and R7 (close rules, including "no close on a two-round hold").
- Unit tests for R11.2 (figures not in the e-mail dropped), R11.8 (prose offer locked in), R11.9-R11.11
  (repair, rebuild on hold, sheet guard), R11.12 (no competitive pressure without a rival), R11.14-R11.15
  (clock) and R11.17-R11.18 (coverage, every RFQ bidder answered).
- Unit tests for R12.2 (coverage lock), R12.4 (revealed slopes), R12.10 (never regress), R12.11 (accept
  ladder order), R12.12 (final offer accepted, one repair only), R12.14 (RFQ message 1 cites the
  rival) and R12.17 (model budget). TeamAgent's offline tests on recorded negotiations
  (`team/tests/test_offline.py`) are the template.
- Unit tests for R13.1-R13.5 (one term per step, option order, reopen, a step needs two packages,
  revealed terms), R13.6 (prose alternatives in English and German), R13.7 (no identical resend),
  R13.8 (equal C within EUR 1, price above the C-minimum with the margin charge), R13.9 (index window,
  a rising index kept out), R13.11 (volatile series), R13.15 (lint) and R13.16 (an RFQ final offer
  accepted inside 60 s).
- Practice runs, the best recorded run per case (`runs/best_runs.json`, `runs/meso3`, `runs/meso4`):
  P01 ≥ 0.941, P02 ≥ 0.507, P03 ≥ 0.919, P04 ≥ 0.86, P05 ≥ 0.781, P07 ≥ 0.773, P08 ≥ 0.549,
  P10 ≥ 0.671, P11 ≥ 0.710, P18 ≥ 0.453 (mean 71.6). The P02 best run (0.507) is in no agent's
  session log and is not TeamAgent's; its e-mails use the shared writer, so it is probably a BuyerAgent
  or DualAgent run with logging off. Treat that target as a stretch goal.
- All 10 practice cases end in a deal (TeamAgent v9 did).
- Every message goes out within 60 s; no `contradicted` claims; no e-mail without a company name;

"""R13.9, R13.11, R13.15: independently computed claims and safe email text."""

import pytest
from spec_support import agent, case, opening

from arena_kit import claims, writing
from arena_kit.spec import email, playbook, sheets
from arena_kit.spec.estimate import Estimate


def index_case(change=-3.7, end="2026-08", start="2025-08", asked=10):
    c = case("case:P08")
    series = next(o["series"] for o in c["term_options"]["index_clause"] if o)
    c["facts"] = {
        f"idx:{series}@{start}": {"value": 100},
        f"idx:{series}@{end}": {"value": 100 * (1 + change / 100)},
        c["trigger_doc"]: {"asked_pct": asked},
    }
    return c, series


def test_r13_9_index_window_rounding_and_case_facts_override_package():
    c, series = index_case(-3.74)
    assert claims.index_change(None, c, series) == (-3.7, f"idx:{series}@2025-08", f"idx:{series}@2026-08")
    c["facts"][f"idx:{series}@2026-10"] = {"value": 999}  # future data must not enter frozen window
    assert claims.index_change(None, c, series)[0] == -3.7
    args = claims.candidates(None, c, c["suppliers"][0], 6)
    claim = next(a for a in args if a.kind == "index")
    assert "-3.7%" in claim.sentence and len(claim.ids) == 2


@pytest.mark.parametrize("start,end", [("2024-08", "2025-08"), ("2025-07", "2026-08")])
def test_r13_9_stale_end_or_more_than_twelve_months_is_not_cited(start, end):
    c, series = index_case(start=start, end=end)
    assert claims.index_change(None, c, series) is None


@pytest.mark.parametrize("change,asked,favourable", [(6, 10, False), (5, 10, False), (4.9, 10, True), (-1, 0, True)])
def test_r13_9_rising_index_only_when_less_than_half_requested_increase(change, asked, favourable):
    c, _ = index_case(change, asked=asked)
    args = claims.candidates(None, c, c["suppliers"][0], 6)
    claim = next(a for a in args if a.kind == "index")
    assert claim.favourable is favourable
    assert (claim in claims.usable(args, claims.Ledger(), "supplier")) is favourable


def test_r13_9_notice_comparison_and_claim_ledger_scope():
    c = case("case:P01")
    ctr = next(ref for ref in c["refs"] if ref.startswith("ctr:"))
    c["facts"] = {c["trigger_doc"]: {"days": 30}, ctr: {"days": 90}}
    notice = next(a for a in claims.candidates(None, c, c["suppliers"][0], 138) if a.kind == "notice")
    assert notice.ids == [c["trigger_doc"], ctr] and "30 days" in notice.sentence
    assert "90 days" in notice.extra[0]
    ledger = claims.Ledger()
    ledger.use(notice, "s1")
    assert ledger.spent(notice, "s2")
    rival = claims.Claim("rival", "rival", ["offer:rival-1"], "A rival offer.")
    ledger.use(rival, "s1")
    assert ledger.spent(rival, "s1") and not ledger.spent(rival, "s2")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("change,volatile", [(15, False), (15.1, True), (-15.1, True)])
def test_r13_11_volatile_series_filters_every_clause_option(change, volatile):
    c, series = index_case(change)
    sid = c["suppliers"][0]
    threads = {sid: [opening(sid, {"unit_price": 6, "payment_days": 60, "contract_months": 24,
                                 "index_clause": None})]}
    a = agent(c, threads)
    # Use only this case's synthetic facts, not the package's additional later month.
    a.package = None
    a._volatile.clear()
    assert a.volatile(series) is volatile
    ctx = sheets.Ctx(c, {}, Estimate(), threads[sid][0]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"], playbook.row(c), a.volatile)
    opts = ctx.allowed("index_clause", ctx.their)
    assert (opts == [None]) is volatile


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sentence", [
    "This is urgent.", "Our deadline is tomorrow.", "Our budget allows this.",
    "We have no other supplier.", "This is single source.", "The line stop would hurt.",
    "Our fallback is weak.", "This is our walk-away price.", "The maximum we can pay is higher.",
    "The best we can pay is in option A.", "This lowers our total cost.", "Our category goal is routine.",
    "This improves our score.", "See cost:310010.", "The price is EUR 999.",
    "We can reduce it by 3%.",  # small invented figures are figures too
])
def test_r13_15_lint_drops_leaks_ids_and_unstated_figures_sentence_by_sentence(sentence):
    dropped = []
    assert writing.lint(f"Thank you for your reply. {sentence}", set(), dropped) == "Thank you for your reply."
    assert len(dropped) == 1


def test_r13_15_keeps_supported_figure_and_known_person_only():
    assert writing.lint("We accept EUR 137.00.", writing.allowed("EUR 137.00")) == "We accept EUR 137.00."
    assert writing.salutation("Dear Anna,", "Foundry GmbH", "Kind regards\nAnna") == "Dear Anna,"
    assert writing.salutation("Dear Invented,", "Foundry GmbH", "Kind regards\nAnna") == \
        "Dear colleagues at Foundry GmbH,"


def test_r13_14_options_match_all_terms_and_code_answers_volume_question():
    terms = {"unit_price": 137, "payment_days": 60, "effective_date": "2027-04-01", "contract_months": 24,
             "volume_per_year": 23400, "lead_time_days": 28, "ppm_commitment": 300,
             "chargeback_eur_per_complaint": 500, "incoterm": "DAP", "tooling_eur": 7500,
             "index_clause": {"series": "TEST", "material_share": 0.5, "deadband_pct": 5, "base_month": "2026-08"}}
    text = email.describe(terms, list(terms))
    for fragment in ("137.00", "60 days", "2027-04-01", "24-month", "23,400", "28 days", "300 ppm",
                     "500 chargeback", "DAP", "7,500", "TEST", "50%", "5%", "2026-08"):
        assert fragment in text
    assert "23,400 units per year over 24 months" in email.commitment(terms)


def test_r13_15_person_in_other_material_is_not_supplier_salutation():
    parts = {"salutation": "Dear Anna,", "opening": "Thank you.", "claims": []}

    assert body.startswith("Dear colleagues at Foundry GmbH,")

  ask only what the need requires.

  one term, that pair is its own price for the term (`revealed_slopes`). With it, a lever counts only
  if it saves us more than the supplier charges for it; on a tie (within EUR 1) take the option closest
  to the supplier's own value - no stricter ask than needed. Its payment slope is its cost of money
  (R2.2).

  15 % is the size of the deadlock-breaking step (R5.3) and the floor of a step we choose to make;

  more to the supplier, so that sheet may go lower. A give worth more than the price room (e.g. half
