item.aggregated_output:
# Tacto Negotiation Arena - starter kit

A Python client for the arena API, two example buyer agents that negotiate by e-mail, helpers that
read the suppliers' documents and price a term sheet, a runner that plays many cases in parallel,
`arena-sim` - a local simulator of the arena's API - and a read-only MCP server over the data
package. Read the brief first
(`../brief/brief.md`); the full API is in `../brief/api.md`. Code: MIT.

## Quickstart - first agent on the board in 15 minutes

You need Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

**1. Get your team's key** (one per team): open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once an organiser approves,
the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page (or its
link) shows it; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it. Keep it out of git.

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --all-extras            # 2. install
cp .env.example .env            # 3. put ARENA_URL and your key (ARENA_API_KEY) into .env
uv run arena me                 # 4. your team and its practice quota
uv run arena cases              # 5. the practice cases (the 10 hosted ones are playable)
uv run arena play case:P01 -v   # 6. the naive agent negotiates one case
uv run arena board              # 7. you are on the practice leaderboard
```

Is the arena up? `curl $ARENA_URL/health`.

Step 6 prints the deal, your total cost `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the case score,
and a **replay link**: every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move, in words. That is
the learning loop - play a practice case, read the replay, improve your agent, play
again. In practice your best score per case counts, so play a case again whenever your agent improves.
**Quota:** 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours. `arena play` and `arena run` print
how many are left; `arena run` plays only the hosted practice cases and stops starting new ones
once the quota is used up (a `429` there does not go away by retrying). Plan your runs.

**Now the LLM agent.** Download the data (`ARENA_DATA=data/package` in `.env`), choose a model in
`.env` (your own key), then:

```bash
uv run arena data                                          # unpacks data/package (and the Sunday release once public)
uv run arena play case:P01 --agent llm -v
uv run arena run --set practice --agent llm --parallel 8   # every hosted practice case, 8 at a time
uv run arena play case:D02 -v                              # the sandbox: 3 demo suppliers, no board
```

**Sunday 08:00:** run `arena data` again - it adds `data/release-sunday` (new news, letters, a
memo). `DataPackage` merges its facts and documents automatically; hidden cases may cite them.

**Master data file:** convert the downloaded package (and an available Sunday release) into one
`master.json` with:

```bash
uv run arena-build-master-data data/package
```

`DataPackage` reads that JSON for lookups, documents, cases and negotiation dossiers. It refreshes
the file automatically when source files change. Its general `query()` method creates a temporary,
read-only in-memory SQLite view from the JSON rows; it does not reopen the source database.

## Hello World (local, 3 commands)

No key yet? Play a whole case against the local simulator - no network, no quota, no LLM costs.
The simulator's supplier is a plain script; the real ones are on arena.tacto.ai. After
`uv sync --all-extras` (step 2 above):

```bash
# terminal 1: the simulator (--data is optional: leave it out until you have run `arena data`)
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package
# terminal 2: a simulator key, then the naive agent plays case:S01
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Hello World" sim                  # prints an api_key
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 ARENA_API_KEY=<the api_key> uv run arena play case:S01 -v
```

It prints the deal, `c_deal` against `c_open` and `c_best`, the score and a replay link - open it
in your browser: the result on top, then every e-mail of the negotiation.

## Try it by hand (Postman, curl)

Feel the API before you put a model in front of it. On the real arena (practice and sandbox) the
60-second rule applies: three late replies in a row end the thread - too fast for typing. **By
hand, use the simulator first**, without the clock:

```bash
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package           # data/package from `arena data`; --data is optional
ARENA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run arena register "Team Name" sim   # prints a simulator api_key
export SIM=http://127.0.0.1:8000 KEY=<the api_key>
```

Every call sends `X-API-Key: <key>`; every `POST` also `Content-Type: application/json` and a
fresh `X-Move-Id` (any unique string - the same id again returns the same answer). In Postman:
those headers, the body as raw JSON.

```bash
# 1. the cases: case:S01 has one supplier, sup:70270, and the negotiable fields unit_price, payment_days
curl -s "$SIM/v1/cases?set=practice" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 2. open a session: the reply carries session_id (sim1 on a fresh simulator) and each supplier's quote e-mail
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Move-Id: open-1" -d '{"case_id": "case:S01"}'

# 3. the supplier's opening e-mail: its term sheet (offer:70270-0) and the quote PDF to fetch
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"

# 4. your e-mail with an offer: the reply is the supplier's answer (status, term_sheets, claim_results)
curl -s -X POST "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270/messages" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Move-Id: msg-1" \
  -d '{"message": {"subject": "Adapter piece HI", "body": "Thank you for your quote. We offer 15.50 EUR at 60 days.",
       "term_sheets": [{"terms": {"unit_price": 15.5, "payment_days": 60}}]}}'

# 5. read the reply in the thread, and the session state
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/threads/sup:70270" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
curl -s "$SIM/v1/sessions/sim1" -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

To close, send `{"message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:70270-1"}}}` (the
term sheet you take) or `{"message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}` to the same `messages` path;
the answer carries the result and score. The quote PDF: `GET $SIM/v1/sessions/sim1/attachments/att:70270-0-quote`.
The same calls work on the arena (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, your team's key, a practice case) - with
the clock running.

## The Live Final: waves, in parallel, within the cap

The final comes in 5 themed waves. A wave holds several hidden cases that appear when the host
starts it; play them all in parallel (up to 10 open sessions per key). Each wave has a hard
cap - **8 minutes** (the host may extend one) - and what is still open then ends without a deal.
Start the runner before the first wave and leave it running:

```bash
uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
```

It polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`, plays every case of a new wave at once (one agent per case),
closes each case **90 seconds before its wave's cap** (read from the wave's `seconds_left`, so an
extension counts) - earlier if a round in that case took longer
(`play.closing_move`: the cheapest standing term
sheet that keeps the must-haves and beats your alternative, else walk away) and stops after the
fifth wave has closed. If it crashes, start it again: it picks up the sessions it had started.
In Python: `play_waves(client, new_agent)`. It reads only your own cases and sessions - during
the final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the screen or the event feed (`arena board`
is for you, not for the agent).

A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds,
and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the
limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a
retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before
Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes.

## Your own agent

An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`.
`threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with
their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an
action that closes the case:

```python
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost
from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing


class Haggler:
    def decide(self, case, threads):
        sid = live_threads(threads)[0]
        events = threads[sid]
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)  # the supplier's standing term sheet
        std = standard_terms(events)  # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing
        if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"):
            return {
                "supplier_id": sid,
                "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
            }
        ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97})
        print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask))
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case["title"],
                "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}],
            },
        }


print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler()))
```

| Module | What |
|---|---|
| `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` |
| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) |
| `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion |
| `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms |
| `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases |
| `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline |
| `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts |
| `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) |
| `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below |

The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
alternative.

**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:

```python
supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
```

## Worked example: cite an index (case P01)

Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the
data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access):

```python
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

pkg = DataPackage("data/package")
# 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate:
pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'")
# -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32
# 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year.
rows = pkg.query(
    "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month"
)
# 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart,
#    ending within the last 12 months of the data.
a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
# 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs.
print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).")
# -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08
#    (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
```

Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure
matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too
old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far,
is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the
replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which
supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent.

A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute; its time never counts against your 60 seconds,
and the client waits up to 180 seconds for a reply. The client paces itself below the
limit of 10 calls per second and retries dropped connections with the same `X-Move-Id`, so a
retry never sends a message twice. Rehearse with `arena run --set practice --parallel 10` (it counts against your quota) before
Sunday, from the machine and network you will use: every case should end well inside 8 minutes.

## Your own agent

An agent is any object with `decide(case, threads) -> {"supplier_id": …, "message": {…}}`.
`threads` holds every e-mail so far per supplier, oldest first; supplier attachments come with
their text under `"text"`. The message is an e-mail - subject, body, up to 3 term sheets - or an
action that closes the case:

```python
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer, play, total_cost
from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import latest, live_threads, standing


class Haggler:
    def decide(self, case, threads):
        sid = live_threads(threads)[0]
        events = threads[sid]
        sheet_id, terms = standing(events)  # the supplier's standing term sheet
        std = standard_terms(events)  # from its quote PDF: what closes if a field is missing
        if latest(events)["status"] in ("agreed", "final_offer"):
            return {
                "supplier_id": sid,
                "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
            }
        ask = complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"] * 0.97})
        print("their C:", total_cost(case, terms, std), "ours:", total_cost(case, ask))
        return {
            "supplier_id": sid,
            "message": {
                "subject": case["title"],
                "body": "Thank you for your quote. Could you send us a cost breakdown?",
                "term_sheets": [{"terms": ask}],
            },
        }


print(play(RemoteTable(ArenaClient()), "case:P01", Haggler()))
```

| Module | What |
|---|---|
| `client.py` | `ArenaClient`: one method per endpoint (messages, threads, attachments, back office, `me`, ...); paced, safe retries; `practice_remaining` |
| `play.py` | `play()`, `play_all()`, `play_waves()` (the Live Final); `RemoteTable` - the hosted arena (practice, sandbox, final) |
| `cost.py` | the published cost function C with the category goal's rates, `supplier_value` for the relationship term, must-haves, term-sheet completion |
| `docs.py` | supplier documents to text (PDF, XLSX); a quote PDF to its offered, standard and fixed terms |
| `data.py` | the data package and the Sunday release: `facts.json`, read-only SQL, lookup by ID, documents, cases |
| `agents/naive.py` | anchors 10 % low, splits the difference, accepts early - the baseline |
| `agents/llm.py` | the model writes the e-mail and the term sheets from the case and the data it points to; code computes C, reads the documents, removes IDs that do not exist, and refuses bad accepts |
| `sim.py` | `arena-sim`: the public API on your machine, with one plain scripted supplier (below) |
| `mcp_server.py` | the MCP server below |

The LLM agent is a starting point, not a winner: it sees only what the case file points to.
Finding the data that moves a supplier is your job - the worked example below shows one way for
one kind of argument. Ideas beyond it: mine the notes and e-mails, read the suppliers' signals and
documents, send two or three term sheets to learn what a supplier values, ask its roles the right
questions, keep RFQ threads alive in parallel, and never leak urgency, a budget or a missing
alternative.

**Strategic and bottleneck cases** (`category_goal` `stabilise` or `secure_supply`) charge C for a
deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin. Pass your estimate of the supplier to
price it - without one, `total_cost` leaves the term out:

```python
supplier = {"full_cost": 128.0, "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}  # your estimate
total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier)
```

## Worked example: cite an index (case P01)

Brandlhuber, a foundry, announces +9.5 % on volute casings and blames energy and wages. Does the
data agree? `DataPackage` reads the package (the MCP server below gives an LLM the same access):

```python
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

pkg = DataPackage("data/package")
# 1. What drives this part's cost? The category team's estimate:
pkg.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = 'part:310010'")
# -> PPI-C241 (iron and steel) 0.26, PPI-D351 (electric power) 0.06, LCI-C (labour) 0.32
# 2. The letter blames energy: read the electricity producer price index for the last year.
rows = pkg.query(
    "SELECT id, month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = 'PPI-D351' AND month >= '2025-08' ORDER BY month"
)
# 3. Compute the change yourself - two months of one series, at most 12 months apart,
#    ending within the last 12 months of the data.
a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
change = (b["value"] / a["value"] - 1) * 100
# 4. One sentence: the figure next to both IDs.
print(f"Electricity producer prices changed {change:+.1f}% from {a['month']} to {b['month']} ({a['id']}, {b['id']}).")
# -> Electricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08
#    (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).
```

Put that sentence into your e-mail and read `claim_results` in the reply: `verified` (the figure
matches the data), `irrelevant` (true, but not about this supplier's costs, or the window is too
old) or `contradicted` (a wrong figure - it costs trust). Whether it moves the price, and how far,
is the supplier's business - a true figure may disarm one supplier and leave the next cold; the
replay shows what it made of it. Which series matter to which
supplier, which window, and what else in the data speaks for you - that is up to your agent.

"""The case clock (R11.14-R11.16) and the model's time budget (R12.17).

From case open: no new counter-offer after NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT, closed by FORCE_CLOSE_AT, so every
case ends inside the 8-minute wave cap. A round (our send to the supplier's reply) is measured per
thread - the last three, each capped at MAX_ROUND_S, DEFAULT_ROUND_S before any is measured - plus
ROUND_MARGIN_S, and no round starts that cannot finish before FORCE_CLOSE_AT. In the final the case
may open with less than 8 minutes left on its wave (`seconds_left`): the two marks move earlier.
"""

import threading
import time

NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT = 360.0
FORCE_CLOSE_AT = 420.0
DEFAULT_ROUND_S = 45.0
MAX_ROUND_S = 90.0
ROUND_MARGIN_S = 10.0
CAP_MARGIN_S = 60.0  # final: closed this long before the wave's cap at the latest
# R12.17: the model gets MODEL_WINDOW_S minus the time since the supplier's reply minus PER_OTHER_S for
# every other thread with a call in flight; under MIN_MODEL_S the planned move goes out without it.
MODEL_WINDOW_S, PER_OTHER_S, MIN_MODEL_S = 50.0, 15.0, 10.0


def model_budget(since_reply_s, others_in_flight):
    """Seconds the writer model may take, or None when the planned move must go without it."""
    budget = MODEL_WINDOW_S - max(0.0, since_reply_s) - PER_OTHER_S * max(0, others_in_flight)
    return budget if budget >= MIN_MODEL_S else None


class CaseClock:
    def __init__(self, seconds_left=None, now=time.monotonic):
        self.now = now
        self.t_open = None
        self.force_close_at, self.no_counter_at = FORCE_CLOSE_AT, NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT
        if isinstance(seconds_left, int | float):
            cap = seconds_left - CAP_MARGIN_S
            if cap < FORCE_CLOSE_AT:
                self.force_close_at = max(0.0, cap)
                self.no_counter_at = max(0.0, cap - (FORCE_CLOSE_AT - NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT))
        self.rounds = []  # measured round times, oldest first
        self._sent = {}  # sid -> when our last message went out
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def open(self):
        if self.t_open is None:
            self.t_open = self.now()
        return self

    def elapsed(self):
        return 0.0 if self.t_open is None else self.now() - self.t_open

    def sent(self, sid):
        with self._lock:
            self._sent[sid] = self.now()

    def replied(self, sid):
        """The supplier answered: one round measured (capped at MAX_ROUND_S)."""
        with self._lock:
            t = self._sent.pop(sid, None)
            if t is not None:
                self.rounds.append(min(self.now() - t, MAX_ROUND_S))

    def round_time(self):
        with self._lock:
            seen = self.rounds[-3:]
        return (max(seen) if seen else DEFAULT_ROUND_S) + ROUND_MARGIN_S

    def can_counter(self):
        """A new counter-offer may still go out: before NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT, and its round fits."""
        e = self.elapsed()
        return e < self.no_counter_at and e + self.round_time() <= self.force_close_at

    def round_fits(self):
        """One more round (e.g. a lock-in of a prose offer) finishes before FORCE_CLOSE_AT."""
        return self.elapsed() + self.round_time() <= self.force_close_at

    def late(self):
        return self.elapsed() >= self.no_counter_at

    def must_close(self):
        return self.elapsed() >= self.force_close_at

    def near_end(self, rounds=2):
        """Fewer than `rounds` rounds left before NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT (R11.8 pressure)."""
        return self.elapsed() + rounds * self.round_time() > self.no_counter_at

def model_budget(since_reply_s, others_in_flight):
    """Seconds the writer model may take, or None when the planned move must go without it."""
    budget = MODEL_WINDOW_S - max(0.0, since_reply_s) - PER_OTHER_S * max(0, others_in_flight)
    return budget if budget >= MIN_MODEL_S else None


class CaseClock:
    def __init__(self, seconds_left=None, now=time.monotonic):
        self.now = now
        self.t_open = None
        self.force_close_at, self.no_counter_at = FORCE_CLOSE_AT, NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT
        if isinstance(seconds_left, int | float):
            cap = seconds_left - CAP_MARGIN_S
            if cap < FORCE_CLOSE_AT:
                self.force_close_at = max(0.0, cap)
                self.no_counter_at = max(0.0, cap - (FORCE_CLOSE_AT - NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT))
        self.rounds = []  # measured round times, oldest first
        self._sent = {}  # sid -> when our last message went out
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def open(self):
        if self.t_open is None:
            self.t_open = self.now()
        return self

    def elapsed(self):
        return 0.0 if self.t_open is None else self.now() - self.t_open

    def sent(self, sid):
        with self._lock:
            self._sent[sid] = self.now()

    def replied(self, sid):
        """The supplier answered: one round measured (capped at MAX_ROUND_S)."""
        with self._lock:
            t = self._sent.pop(sid, None)
            if t is not None:
                self.rounds.append(min(self.now() - t, MAX_ROUND_S))

    def round_time(self):
        with self._lock:
            seen = self.rounds[-3:]
        return (max(seen) if seen else DEFAULT_ROUND_S) + ROUND_MARGIN_S

    def can_counter(self):
        """A new counter-offer may still go out: before NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT, and its round fits."""
        e = self.elapsed()
        return e < self.no_counter_at and e + self.round_time() <= self.force_close_at

    def round_fits(self):
        """One more round (e.g. a lock-in of a prose offer) finishes before FORCE_CLOSE_AT."""
        return self.elapsed() + self.round_time() <= self.force_close_at

    def late(self):
        return self.elapsed() >= self.no_counter_at

    def must_close(self):
        return self.elapsed() >= self.force_close_at

    def near_end(self, rounds=2):
        """Fewer than `rounds` rounds left before NO_NEW_COUNTER_AT (R11.8 pressure)."""
        return self.elapsed() + rounds * self.round_time() > self.no_counter_at

"""R11.14–R11.15, R12.17 and R13.16: virtual time, no real sleeps."""

from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from arena_kit.spec import runner
from arena_kit.spec.clock import CaseClock, model_budget


class Time:
    def __init__(self, value=0.0):
        self.value = value

    def monotonic(self):
        return self.value

    def sleep(self, seconds):
        self.value += seconds


def test_r11_14_no_counter_at_360_and_force_close_at_420():
    time = Time(100)
    clock = CaseClock(now=time.monotonic).open()
    time.value = 459
    assert clock.can_counter()
    time.value = 460
    assert clock.late() and not clock.can_counter() and clock.round_fits()
    time.value = 520
    assert clock.must_close() and not clock.round_fits()
    clock.open()  # opening twice must not reset the case clock
    assert clock.elapsed() == 420


def test_r11_15_rounds_use_last_three_capped_at_90_plus_margin():
    time = Time()
    clock = CaseClock(now=time.monotonic).open()
    assert clock.round_time() == 55
    for seconds in (120, 10, 20, 30):
        clock.sent("supplier")
        time.sleep(seconds)
        clock.replied("supplier")
    assert clock.rounds == [90, 10, 20, 30]
    assert clock.round_time() == 40
    time.value = 350
    clock.rounds = [90]
    assert not clock.can_counter()  # round would end at 450, despite being before 360
    assert not clock.round_fits()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seconds_left,no_counter,force", [(480, 360, 420), (240, 120, 180), (30, 0, 0), (0, 0, 0)])
def test_wave_clock_shortens_to_actual_remaining_time(seconds_left, no_counter, force):
    clock = CaseClock(seconds_left)
    assert (clock.no_counter_at, clock.force_close_at) == (no_counter, force)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("elapsed,others,expected", [(0, 0, 50), (10, 1, 25), (10, 2, 10), (10.1, 2, None)])
def test_r12_17_writer_budget(elapsed, others, expected):
    assert model_budget(elapsed, others) == expected


def test_r13_16_accept_wait_does_not_exceed_reply_clock(monkeypatch):
    time = Time(20)
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "time", time)
    runner.wait_for_rivals({"best": False, "slow": True}, "best", {"best": 0})
    assert time.value == 45  # 15 seconds remain to send the accept
    runner.wait_for_rivals({"slow": True}, "best", {"best": 0})
    assert time.value == 45  # expired budget must not restart on a second attempt


def test_r13_16_does_not_wait_for_own_call_or_completed_rivals(monkeypatch):
    time = Time(5)
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "time", time)
    runner.wait_for_rivals({"best": True, "other": False}, "best", {"best": 0})
    assert time.value == 5


def test_r13_16_slow_post_recovers_already_visible_reply(monkeypatch):
    from concurrent.futures import TimeoutError
    from importlib import import_module

    play = import_module("arena_kit.play")
    reply = {"from": "supplier", "status": "final_offer"}

    class Pending:
        def result(self, timeout):
            assert timeout <= 3  # polling must leave almost the entire 60-second reply budget
            raise TimeoutError

        def done(self):
            return False

    monkeypatch.setattr(play, "SENDER", SimpleNamespace(submit=lambda *args: Pending()))
    client = SimpleNamespace(send_message=lambda *args: None)
    table = play.RemoteTable(client)
    reads = iter([[{"from": "supplier"}], [{"from": "supplier"}, {"from": "buyer"}, reply]])
    monkeypatch.setattr(table, "refresh", lambda sid: next(reads))
    assert table.send("supplier", {"body": "offer"}) is reply

"""The published cost function: what a term sheet costs the buyer in €, plus term helpers.

C covers the buyer's fixed need over a fixed horizon: need the deal does not cover is bought at
the case's fallback price (plus the fallback risk of the category goal), committed volume is bought
needed or not, and units bought before a new price takes effect cost the current price. In
strategic and bottleneck cases a deal that leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin costs
too - pass your estimate of the supplier (`supplier_value`) to price that. Do the arithmetic here,
not in the language model.
"""

import math
import operator
from datetime import date

# Strategic and bottleneck goals: leaving the supplier below a sustainable margin costs.
RELATIONSHIP_GOALS = {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}
OPS = {
    "<=": operator.le,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    ">": operator.gt,
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
}


def closing_terms(case, terms, standard=None):
    """The terms a deal would close on: the term sheet, then the supplier's standard terms (from
    its quote PDF) for anything left out, then the case's fixed terms; gaps from the buyer's plan.
    """
    b = case["buyer"]
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan = {
        "volume_per_year": b["need_per_year"],
        "contract_months": round(12 * b["horizon_years"]),
        "payment_days": b["reference_payment_days"],
        "lead_time_days": b["need_lead_time_days"],
        # an unknown Incoterm counts as the costliest: a cautious buyer does not assume DAP
        "incoterm": max(freight, key=freight.get),
    }
    t = dict(plan)
    for layer in (standard or {}, case.get("fixed_terms", {}), terms):
        t.update({k: v for k, v in layer.items() if v is not None or k not in plan})
    return t


def horizon_start(case):
    """The horizon starts at the fixed or the earliest possible effective date."""
    fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {}).get("effective_date")
    options = [o for o in case.get("term_options", {}).get("effective_date", []) if o]
    first = fixed or (min(options) if options else None)
    return date.fromisoformat(first) if first else None


def _years(case, t):
    """Years of the horizon a deal covers; a single order (0 months) counts as one year's lot.
    A commitment beyond the horizon neither costs nor earns."""
    months = t["contract_months"]
    return min(months / 12 if months else 1.0, case["buyer"]["horizon_years"])


def _units_before(case, t, years):
    """Units bought between the horizon start and the date a new price takes effect."""
    start = horizon_start(case)
    if not t.get("effective_date") or start is None:
        return 0.0
    lag = (date.fromisoformat(t["effective_date"]) - start).days / 365
    return t["volume_per_year"] * min(max(lag, 0.0), years)


def supplier_value(case, terms, supplier):
    """What a deal is worth to the supplier per unit, in cash: the price at its standard terms that
    would pay it the same. `supplier` is your estimate of it:
      standard       its standard terms (quote PDF, `docs.standard_terms`)
      interest_rate  what money now is worth to it per year (more to a supplier short of cash)
      usual_rate     its usual cost of money (default: interest_rate); tooling paid up front is
                     worth more to it when cash is dearer than usual
      ppm            the defect rate it really achieves (default: its standard ppm commitment)
      extra          EUR per unit it gains (+) or spends (-) beyond these items, e.g. overtime for
                     a faster delivery or idle capacity a larger volume fills (default 0)
    Contract length and an index clause are security, not cash: they do not count here."""
    b, std = case["buyer"], {**supplier["standard"], **case.get("fixed_terms", {})}
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, std)
    years = _years(case, t)
    sold = t["volume_per_year"] * years
    old = _units_before(case, t, years) / sold  # sold at the current price
    rate = supplier["interest_rate"]
    pay = 1 - rate * (t["payment_days"] - std["payment_days"]) / 360
    cash_now = 1 + (rate - supplier.get("usual_rate", rate)) * years / 2
    freight = b["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    ppm = supplier.get("ppm", std.get("ppm_commitment") or 0)
    return (
        t["unit_price"] * (1 - old) * pay
        + old * (b.get("current_unit_price") or 0.0) * pay
        + freight[t["incoterm"]]
        - freight[std["incoterm"]]  # it carries the freight leg
        + ((t.get("tooling_eur") or 0) - (std.get("tooling_eur") or 0)) / sold * cash_now
        - ppm / 1e6 * ((t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0) - (std.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0))
        + supplier.get("extra", 0.0)
    )


def _soft(gap):
    """Margin points below the sustainable margin, as they cost: none above it, quadratic over
    the first 5 points, linear beyond - no kink."""
    if gap <= 0:
        return 0.0
    return gap * gap / 10 if gap <= 5 else gap - 2.5


def relationship_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None, value=None):
    """Strategic and bottleneck goals only: EUR for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier
    below `sustainable_margin_pct`, per year covered. `supplier["full_cost"]` (EUR per unit) is your
    estimate of its full cost; `value` overrides `supplier_value`. Without an estimate: 0."""
    b = case["buyer"]
    per_point, sustainable = b.get("relationship_eur_per_point"), b.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
    if b.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not per_point or not sustainable or not supplier:
        return 0.0
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    worth = value if value is not None else supplier_value(case, t, supplier)
    margin = (worth - supplier["full_cost"]) / worth * 100
    return per_point * _soft(sustainable - margin) * _years(case, t)


def cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C by part. `standard`: the supplier's standard terms for anything the term sheet leaves out.
    `supplier`: your estimate of the supplier for the relationship term (`supplier_value`)."""
    b, t = case["buyer"], closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    if t.get("unit_price") is None:
        raise ValueError("no unit_price: a term sheet without a price has no cost")
    years = _years(case, t)
    committed = t["volume_per_year"] * years  # bought, needed or not
    covered = min(t["volume_per_year"], b["need_per_year"]) * years
    pre = _units_before(case, t, years)
    at_new_price = (committed - pre) * t["unit_price"]
    spend = pre * (b.get("current_unit_price") or t["unit_price"]) + at_new_price
    per_defect = b.get("cost_per_defect", 0)
    defect_cost = per_defect - min(t.get("chargeback_eur_per_complaint") or 0, per_defect)
    index = index_risk = 0.0
    if clause := t.get("index_clause"):
        path = b.get("index_paths", {}).get(clause["series"], 0.0)
        moved = max(0.0, abs(path) - clause["deadband_pct"] / 100)
        index = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * moved * math.copysign(1, path)
        index_risk = at_new_price * clause["material_share"] * b.get("index_risk_pct", 0) / 100
    uncovered = (b["need_per_year"] * b["horizon_years"] - covered) * b["fallback_unit_price"]
    need = b["need_lead_time_days"]
    return {
        "price": spend,
        "uncovered_need": uncovered,
        "fallback_risk": uncovered * b.get("fallback_risk_pct", 0) / 100,
        "payment_terms": spend * b["interest_rate"] * (b["reference_payment_days"] - t["payment_days"]) / 360,
        "freight": committed * b["freight_eur_per_unit"][t["incoterm"]],
        "late_delivery": b.get("late_cost_per_day", 0) * max(0, t["lead_time_days"] - need),
        "quality": committed * (t.get("ppm_commitment") or 0) / 1e6 * defect_cost,
        "tooling": t.get("tooling_eur") or 0.0,
        "index_clause": index,
        "index_risk": index_risk,
        "relationship": relationship_cost(case, t, supplier=supplier),
    }


def total_cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
    """C in EUR; infinite for terms without a price (e.g. a supplier that quotes none), so such a
    sheet is never the cheapest and never beats an alternative."""
    if closing_terms(case, terms, standard).get("unit_price") is None:
        return math.inf
    return round(sum(cost_breakdown(case, terms, standard, supplier).values()), 2)


def score(c_open, c_deal, c_best):
    if c_deal is None:
        return 0.0
    if c_open - c_best <= 0.01:  # no room to negotiate: matching the best is full marks
        return 1.0 if c_deal <= c_best + 0.01 else 0.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, (c_open - c_deal) / (c_open - c_best)))


def must_haves_ok(case, terms, standard=None):
    t = closing_terms(case, terms, standard)
    for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []):
        value = t.get(m["field"])
        if value is None and m["op"] not in ("==", "!="):
            return False
        if not OPS[m["op"]](value, m["value"]):
            return False
    return True


def snap(case, field, value):
    """The allowed value closest to `value` (case `term_options`), else `value` unchanged."""
    options = case.get("term_options", {}).get(field)
    if not options or value in options:
        return value
    if isinstance(value, int | float) and all(isinstance(o, int | float) for o in options):
        return min(options, key=lambda o: (abs(o - value), o))
    return options[0]


def complete_offer(case, terms):
    """A valid term sheet: exactly the negotiable fields, gaps from the buyer's plan, snapped."""
    plan = closing_terms(case, {"unit_price": None})
    freight = case["buyer"]["freight_eur_per_unit"]
    plan["incoterm"] = min(freight, key=freight.get)  # when asking, ask for the cheapest freight
    out = {}
    for field in case["negotiable"]:
        value = terms.get(field, plan.get(field))
        if value is None and case.get("term_options", {}).get(field):
            value = case["term_options"][field][0]
        value = snap(case, field, value)
        out[field] = round(value, 2) if field == "unit_price" and value is not None else value
    return out

"""Term sheets: surplus (R6.2), ask sheets (R6.3), decoy (R6.4), floor (R6.5), repair (R11.9), rebuild
on hold (R11.10), the guard (R11.11), coverage lock (R12.2), payment probe (R12.7), never regress
(R12.10) and exact prices (R13.8)."""

import pytest
from spec_support import CASES, PKG, case

from arena_kit.cost import must_haves_ok, total_cost
from arena_kit.spec import estimate as est_mod
from arena_kit.spec import playbook, pricing, sheets
from arena_kit.spec.terms import complete


def ctx_for(c, their, std=None, est=None):
    their = complete(c, their, std or {})
    est = est or est_mod.estimate(c, PKG, [], their)
    return sheets.Ctx(c, std or {}, est, their, playbook.row(c))


def leverage_ctx():
    c = case("case:P01", category_goal="leverage")  # no margin charge: C is linear in the price
    return c, ctx_for(c, {"unit_price": 138.55, "effective_date": "2026-11-01", "payment_days": 30})


# --- R13.8 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_price_solves_the_target_exactly_without_margin_charge():
    c, ctx = leverage_ctx()
    combo = {k: v for k, v in ctx.their.items() if k != "unit_price"}
    target = ctx.c(ctx.their) * 0.97
    p = pricing.price_for(c, combo, {}, target)
    assert abs(total_cost(c, {**combo, "unit_price": p}) - target) <= pricing.tolerance(c, combo)


def test_step_packages_cost_the_same_within_the_cent_tolerance():
    """R13.8: every sheet of a step has the same C (EUR 1, or half a cent per committed unit)."""
    from arena_kit.spec.steps import Steps

    c, ctx = leverage_ctx()
    base = {k: v for k, v in ctx.their.items() if k != "unit_price"}
    target = ctx.c(ctx.their) * 0.97
    pk = Steps().packages(ctx, "payment_days", base, target, 0.0)
    assert len(pk) >= 2
    tol = pricing.tolerance(c, base)
    assert tol < 50  # 8,150 units: whole cents land within EUR 41
    for _, t in pk:
        assert abs(ctx.c(t) - target) <= tol


def test_with_margin_charge_the_price_sits_above_the_cheapest_price():
    """R13.8: C is convex in the price with the margin charge; the solved price is on the side above
    the C-minimising price."""
    c = CASES["case:P01"]  # stabilise
    ctx = ctx_for(c, {"unit_price": 138.55, "effective_date": "2026-11-01"})
    sup = ctx.supplier
    assert sup is not None
    combo = {k: v for k, v in ctx.their.items() if k != "unit_price"}
    low = pricing.cheapest_price(c, combo, {}, sup, 138.55)
    c_low = total_cost(c, {**combo, "unit_price": low}, {}, sup)
    assert total_cost(c, {**combo, "unit_price": low - 3}, {}, sup) > c_low  # below it C rises again
    target = c_low + 20_000
    p = pricing.price_for(c, combo, {}, target, sup, 138.55)
    assert p > low
    assert abs(total_cost(c, {**combo, "unit_price": p}, {}, sup) - target) <= pricing.tolerance(c, combo)
    assert pricing.price_for(c, combo, {}, c_low - 50_000, sup, 138.55) is None  # out of reach


# --- R6.2 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_give_price_shares_the_surplus():
    assert sheets.give_price(100.0, 96.0) == 98.0  # halfway to the supplier's indifference price
    assert sheets.give_price(100.0, 101.0) == 100.0  # worth less to it than to us: equal cost
    assert sheets.give_price(100.0, None) == 100.0
    assert sheets.give_price(None, 96.0) is None


def test_faster_payment_to_a_cash_short_supplier_is_a_shared_gain():
    """R6.2: at a 14 % cost of money paying 30 days earlier is worth more to it than to us (8 %)."""
    c, ctx = leverage_ctx()
    ctx.est.rate = 0.14
    ref = {k: v for k, v in ctx.their.items() if k != "unit_price"}
    ref["payment_days"] = 60
    give = {**ref, "payment_days": 30}
    p_ind = sheets.indifference_price(ctx, give, ref, 130.0)
    p_eq = pricing.price_for(c, give, {}, ctx.c({**ref, "unit_price": 130.0}))
    assert p_ind < p_eq

"""Contract tests: the kit's client and both example agents against arena-sim over HTTP - and
against a hosted arena when ARENA_TEST_URL and ARENA_TEST_KEY are set."""

import json
import os
import secrets
import sys
import time

import httpx
import pytest

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError, RemoteTable, play, play_all
from arena_kit.agents import LLMAgent, NaiveAgent
from arena_kit.docs import quote_terms
from arena_kit.play import fetch_documents, play_waves

RESULT = {"ended", "deal", "supplier_id", "offer_id", "terms", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "score"}


def team(url, code="sim"):
    key = ArenaClient(url).register(f"test-{secrets.token_hex(3)}", code)["api_key"]
    return ArenaClient(url, key, rate=1000)


def scripted(system, user):
    """A stand-in model: lowballs on the first live thread, accepts once the supplier stops."""
    sid = ":".join(user.split("THREAD ")[1].split(":")[:2])
    stop = any(f"status {s}" in user for s in ("final_offer", "agreed"))
    if stop or user.count("--- buyer") >= 8:
        return json.dumps({"supplier_id": sid, "action": "accept"})
    body = "Thank you. Could you send a cost breakdown?"
    return json.dumps({"supplier_id": sid, "action": "send", "body": body, "term_sheets": [{"unit_price": 1.0}]})


@pytest.fixture(params=["sim", "hosted"])
def arena(request):
    if request.param == "hosted":
        url, key = os.environ.get("ARENA_TEST_URL"), os.environ.get("ARENA_TEST_KEY")
        if not (url and key):
            pytest.skip("set ARENA_TEST_URL and ARENA_TEST_KEY to run against a hosted arena")
        return ArenaClient(url, key), 1
    url, _, _ = request.getfixturevalue("sim")
    return team(url), 3


def test_both_agents_play_unchanged(arena):
    client, n = arena
    for case in client.cases("practice")[:n]:
        for agent in (NaiveAgent(), LLMAgent(scripted)):
            result = play(RemoteTable(client), case["case_id"], agent)
            assert RESULT <= set(result) and result["ended"]
            assert result["score"] is None or 0 <= result["score"] <= 1


def test_naive_is_deterministic_and_play_all_runs_in_parallel(sim):
    client = team(sim[0])
    ids = [c["case_id"] for c in client.cases()]
    first = play_all(lambda: RemoteTable(client), ids + ["case:NOPE"], NaiveAgent)
    second = play_all(lambda: RemoteTable(client), ids, NaiveAgent)
    assert all(first[i] == second[i] and first[i]["deal"] for i in ids)
    assert isinstance(first["case:NOPE"], ArenaError) and first["case:NOPE"].status == 404


def test_documents_follow_the_arena_format(sim):
    client, table = team(sim[0]), None
    table = RemoteTable(client)
    case, threads = table.open("case:S03")
    sup, [opening] = next(iter(threads.items()))
    terms = quote_terms(fetch_documents(table, opening)["attachments"][0]["text"])
    assert terms["stated"] == opening["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]
    assert set(terms["standard"]) == set(opening["missing_fields"])
    assert terms["fixed"]["lead_time_days"] == case["fixed_terms"]["lead_time_days"]
    reply = table.send(sup, {"body": "Could you send a cost breakdown? (idx:NOPE@2026-01)", "term_sheets": []})
    assert reply["claim_results"] == [{"index": 0, "result": "contradicted"}]  # an ID the data lacks
    assert "=SUM(B2:B5)" in fetch_documents(table, reply)["attachments"][0]["text"]


def test_a_rival_quote_counts_once_per_supplier_the_rest_once_per_case(sim):
    url, state, _ = sim
    state.facts["quote:9001"] = {"unit_price": 100.0}  # a rival's quote the buyer holds
    table = RemoteTable(team(url))
    _, threads = table.open("case:S02")
    a, b = threads
    rival = threads[a][0]["term_sheets"][0]["term_sheet_id"]  # a's opening, an offer: ID

    def cite(sup, ids):
        reply = table.send(sup, {"body": f"Please consider {', '.join(ids)}.", "term_sheets": []})
        return [r["result"] for r in reply["claim_results"]]

    assert cite(a, ["quote:9001", "idx:PPI-C241@2026-08"]) == ["verified", "verified"]
    assert cite(b, ["quote:9001", "idx:PPI-C241@2026-08", rival]) == ["verified", "duplicate", "verified"]
    assert cite(b, ["quote:9001", rival, "idx:NOPE@2026-01"]) == ["duplicate", "duplicate", "contradicted"]
    assert cite(b, ["idx:NOPE@2026-01"]) == ["contradicted"]  # an unknown ID never becomes a duplicate


def test_errors_limits_and_retries(sim):
    url, state, _ = sim
    client = team(url)
    assert httpx.get(f"{url}/health").json()["ok"]

  have checked out so far; our last two e-mails; how far it moved toward us in % since our last

    show, give one concrete reason or ask what would let them move;
  - step: "a modest step - this costs us and we expect a step back."

  asked or received - an open supplier sends one, and R2.1 uses it), then the case type's question

+were repeated cleanly. Simulator scores test plumbing, not hosted negotiation quality.

+are compared at three decimals because the requirements round historical raw scores.

+below target. Its wall time includes pre-open profiling; closure from open was about 203 seconds.
+It is a targeted retest, not a replacement ten-case mean.
+
+Raw scores, threads, sessions, audit records, prompts/replies and source fingerprints:
+[model sweep](runs/spec-practice-model/summary.md),
+[final code-only sweep](runs/spec-practice-verified/summary.md),
+[P05 retest](runs/spec-practice-p05-lead-fix/P05.json).

+|---|---|---|

Model play also locked 30-day payment and a January date after the supplier priced an alternative; its cheaper alternative ID was refused by the arena. | Removed the unit-price ceiling while preserving total-cost/floor guards; enforced real choices after guards and persistent revealed locks. Code play improved from 0.759845 to 0.827854 and obtained April, but at EUR 136.85/30 days rather than historical EUR 135.20/60 days. Model play still missed. |
+| P03 | Full coverage is correct. The first credible payment choices at the estimated convex-cost target were 30/45 days; the supplier chose 45 and held EUR 430.09. Historical target play achieved 90 days at EUR 432.29. | Fixed inherited prose slopes and actual-price locks. Repeated code/model games still scored 0.864105. The remaining gap is payment/anchor calibration, not a missing coverage or arithmetic fix. |
+| P05 | Quote-PDF defaults carried unnecessary 28-day expedited delivery despite a 35-day need. Suppliers explicitly state that 28 days costs overtime. Dralveck countered at EUR 28, then walked after another low counter; Fuchsreiter became the remaining best deal. | Relax cost-neutral expedited lead times without violating must-haves; bounded accept waiting and skipped model grace on terminal replies. Model score improved 0.521725 → 0.573210. The anchor/concession path still fails to secure the historical EUR 28.42 deal. |
+| P07 | Correct 24-month coverage/90-day payment, but supplier stopped at EUR 5.46 with the model and EUR 5.40 without it, against historical EUR 5.37. | Retested after lock/guard/no-resend fixes. Final offers were accepted promptly, not countered past withdrawal. Further opening/wording calibration remains unproven; no numerical bug was found that explains the residual price gap. |
+| P08 | Supplier insisted on an index clause; wider deadband menus incurred a price premium and quickly reached final. Model EUR 5.67/5% band differs from historical EUR 5.47/5% band. | Added demanded-series/deadband filtering and persistent revealed-price locks. Code obtained EUR 5.49/0% band and 0.393752; model scored 0.332313. This policy change did not close the gap and some experiments worsened the score. |
+| P10 | Coverage/must-have repair held, but the supplier immediately made a valid final offer: EUR 31.90 with model, EUR 31.70 without, versus historical EUR 31.60. | Verified full 23,400 annual volume/24 months and immediate final acceptance. No unsafe counter after final was used to chase the score. Opening lead-time/price calibration remains a strategy gap. |
+| P18 | Payment/index sequencing left EUR 5.60/0% band with model or EUR 5.80/5% band in code play. Cheaper historical/alternative IDs were refused, then the current offer was accepted. | Retested the deadband/lock changes and robust accept ladder. Best observed score in this work was 0.319096, not 0.453; the wider-band experiment regressed. Payment/deadband premium calibration remains unresolved. |
+
+These causes distinguish observed supplier behaviour from inferred tuning opportunities. A passing
+unit test does not prove a negotiation will reach a historical score, and cross-run differences do
+not establish that model wording alone caused the difference.
+
+## Timing, claims, and consistency review
+
+All ten model cases ended in deals, all returned `must_haves_ok: true`, and all closed before 420
+seconds (maximum 322.0). There were **no contradicted claims** and **no buyer emails missing the
+Hollerau company signature** in the corrected simulator, sandbox or hosted evidence. Model writer
+calls in the ten-case sweep took at most 11.7 seconds, with no writer errors.
+
+The model P05 sweep and its lead-time retest each contain one structured timeout on the deliberately
+idled, uncompetitive Hrvelec thread. An earlier code-only baseline also timed out a Fuchsreiter reply.
+These are not clean passes of the literal every-reply-within-60-seconds acceptance rule. The runner
+now polls slow POSTs after 3 seconds, waits for rivals no longer than 45 seconds after its own reply,
+and refreshes on refused accepts. The remaining idle-bidder timing policy conflict is explicit.
+Hosted records lack per-email delivery timestamps, so absence of timeout records is evidence, not a
+proof of an exact maximum end-to-end reply latency.
+
+[DESIGN_NOTES.md](DESIGN_NOTES.md) collects precedence and judgement calls. Important deviations:
+whole-cent quantization prevents literal EUR 1 equal-cost precision on large lots; opening-price-only
+cost estimates are exempted from the inherited full-cost anchor/floor; and voluntarily idling an RFQ
+bidder can conflict with literal universal reply timing. The demanded-index/revealed-price policy
+also needs further performance tuning. None is silently counted as full requirement compliance.
+
+No final-wave sessions were started, no unrelated user files were removed, and no commit was made.
+The completed artifacts are ready for review, but score/timing acceptance is not yet fully achieved.
*** End Patch"));
